According to his own statement (Luke 1:2), he was not an “eye-witness and minister of the word from the beginning.” It is probable that he was a physician in Troas, and was there converted by Paul, to whom he attached himself. He accompanied him to Philippi, but did not there share his imprisonment, nor did he accompany him further after his release in his missionary journey at this time (Acts 17:1). On Paul’s third visit to Philippi (20:5, 6) we again meet with Luke, who probably had spent all the intervening time in that city, a period of seven or eight years. From this time Luke was Paul’s constant…

name: Maaseiah
summary: The father of the priest Zephaniah (Jer. 21:1; 37:3).

name: Machir
summary: A descendant of the preceding, residing at Lo-debar, where he maintained Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth till he was taken under the care of David (2 Sam. 9:4), and where he afterwards gave shelter to David himself when he was a fugitive (17:27).

name: Malluch
summary: A priest who returned from Babylon (Neh. 12:2).

name: Mamre
summary: An Amoritish chief in alliance with Abraham (Gen. 14:13, 24).

name: Memucan
summary: Dignified, one of the royal counsellors at the court of Ahasuerus, by whose suggestion Vashti was divorced (Esther 1:14, 16, 21).

name: Michah
summary: The first in rank of the priests of the family of Kohathites (1 Chr. 23:20).

name: Mikloth
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:32; 9:37, 38).

name: Miniamin
summary: A chief priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5), called Mijamin (10:7) and Miniamin (12:17).

name: Moadiah
summary: A priest (Neh. 10:8).

name: Mother of the Wife of Simon
Naamah
summary: The daughter of the king of Ammon, one of the wives of Solomon, the only one who appears to have borne him a son, viz., Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:21, 31).

name: Nahash
summary: King of the Ammonites in the time of Saul. The inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead having been exposed to great danger from Nahash, sent messengers to Gibeah to inform Saul of their extremity. He promptly responded to the call, and gathering together an army he marched against Nahash. “And it came to pass that they which remained were scattered, so that two of them [the Ammonites] were not left together” (1 Sam. 11:1-11).

name: Nahath
summary: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau (Gen. 36:13, 17).

name: Nahath
summary: A Kohathite Levite (1 Chr. 6:26).

name: Obadiah
summary: A Levite, after the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:16).

name: Omar
summary: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son (Gen. 36:11-15).

name: Pekahiah
summary: The Lord opened his eyes, the son and successor of Menahem on the throne of Israel. He was murdered in the royal palace of Samaria by Pekah, one of the captains of his army (2 Kings 15:23-26), after a reign of two years (B.C. 761-759). He “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”

name: Phichol
summary: Great, the chief captain of the army of Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar. He entered into an alliance with Abraham with reference to a certain well which, from this circumstance, was called Beersheba (q.v.), “the well of the oath” (Gen. 21:22, 32; 26:26).

name: Philip
summary: Mentioned only in connection with the imprisonment of John the Baptist (Matt. 14:3; Mark 6:17; Luke 3:19). He was the son of Herod the Great, and the first husband of Herodias, and the father of Salome. (See HEROD PHILIP I.)

name: Phut
summary: One of the sons of Ham (Gen. 10:6).

name: Rehabiah
summary: Enlargement of the Lord, the son of Eliezer, and grandson of Moses (1 Chr. 23:17; 24:21).

name: Rimmon
summary: A man of Beeroth (2 Sam. 4:2), one of the four Gibeonite cities. (See Josh. 9:17.)

name: Serah
summary: Abundance; princess, the daughter of Asher and grand-daughter of Jacob (Gen. 46:17); called also Sarah (Num. 26:46; R.V., “Serah”).

name: Shalmaneser
summary: An Assyrian king (Hos. 10:14), identified with Shalmaneser II. (Sayce) or IV. (Lenormant), the successor of Pul on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 728). He made war against Hoshea, the king of Israel, whom he subdued and compelled to pay an annual tribute. Hoshea, however, soon after rebelled against his Assyrian conquerer. Shalmaneser again marched against Samaria, which, after a siege of three years, was taken (2 Kings 17:3-5; 18:9) by Sargon (q.v.). A revolution meantime had broken out in Assyria, and Shalmaneser was deposed. Sargon usurped the vacant throne. Schrader thinks that this is probably the name of a king of Moab mentioned on an inscription of Tiglath-pileser as Salamanu.

name: Shammah
summary: One of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:13, 17).

name: Shammua
summary: One of David’s sons by Bathsheba (1 Chr. 3:5); called also Shammua (14:4).

name: Shebaniah
summary: Another Levite (Neh. 9:4, 5).

name: Shebaniah
summary: A priest who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3; marg., or Shebaniah).

name: Shemaiah
summary: The eldest son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4-8).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A false prophet who opposed Jeremiah (Jer. 29:24-32).

name: Shemiramoth
summary: A Levite in David’s time (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Shephatiah
summary: Ezra 2:4.

name: Shimron
summary: Watchman, the fourth son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13; 1 Chr. 7:1; R.V., correctly, “Shimron”).

name: Shobab
summary: One of David’s sons by Bathseheba (2 Sam. 5:14).

name: Shuah
summary: A Canaanite whose daughter was married to Judah (1 Chr. 2:3).

name: Shubael
summary: One of the descendants of Gershom, who had charge of the temple treasures in the time of David (1 Chr. 23:16; 26:24).

name: Simon
summary: A Jew of Cyrene, in North Africa, then a province of Libya. A hundred thousand Jews from Palestine had been settled in this province by Ptolemy Soter (B.C. 323-285), where by this time they had greatly increased in number. They had a synagogue in Jerusalem for such of their number as went thither to the annual feasts. Simon was seized by the soldiers as the procession wended its way to the place of crucifixion as he was passing by, and the heavy cross which Christ from failing strength could no longer bear was laid on his shoulders. Perhaps they seized him because he showed sympathy with Jesus. He was the “father of Alexander and Rufus” (Matt. 27:32). Possibly this Simon may have been one…

name: Stephanas
summary: Crown, a member of the church at Corinth, whose family were among those the apostle had baptized (1 Cor. 1:16; 16:15, 17). He has been supposed by some to have been the “jailer of Philippi” (comp. Acts 16:33). The First Epistle to the Corinthians was written from Philippi some six years after the jailer’s conversion, and he was with the apostle there at that time.

name: Talmai
summary: One of the Anakim of Hebron, who were slain by the men of Judah under Caleb (Num. 13:22; Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

name: Talmai
summary: A king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after he had put Amnon to death (2 Sam. 3:3; 13:37). His daughter, Maachah, was one of David’s wives, and the mother of Absalom (1 Chr. 3:2).

name: Trophimus
summary: A foster-child, an Ephesian who accompanied Paul during a part of his third missionary journey (Acts 20:4; 21:29). He was with Paul in Jerusalem, and the Jews, supposing that the apostle had brought him with him into the temple, raised a tumult which resulted in Paul’s imprisonment. (See TEMPLE, HEROD’S.) In writing to Timothy, the apostle says, “Trophimus have I left at Miletum sick” (2 Tim. 4:20). This must refer to some event not noticed in the Acts.

name: Urijah
summary: The father of Meremoth, mentioned in Ezra 8:33.

name: Urijah
summary: A prophet of Kirjath-jearim in the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah (Jer. 26:20-23). He fled into Egypt from the cruelty of the king, but having been brought back he was beheaded and his body “cast into the graves of the common people.”

name: Wife of Simon
mother: Mother of the Wife of Simon

name: Zacchaeus
summary: Pure, a superintendant of customs; a chief tax-gather (publicanus) at Jericho (Luke 19:1-10). “The collection of customs at Jericho, which at this time produced and exported a considerable quantity of balsam, was undoubtedly an important post, and would account for Zacchaeus being a rich man.” Being short of stature, he hastened on before the multitude who were thronging about Christ as he passed through Jericho on his way to Jerusalem, and climbed up a sycamore tree that he might be able to see him. When our Lord reached the spot he looked up to the publican among the branches, and addressing him by name, told him to make haste and come down, as he intended that day to abide at his house.…

name: Zaccur
summary: A son of Asaph, and chief of one of the courses of singers as arranged by David (1 Chr. 25:2, 10).

name: Zachariah
summary: Son of Jeroboam II., king of Israel. On the death of his father there was an interregnum of ten years, at the end of which he succeeded to the throne, which he occupied only six months, having been put to death by Shallum, who usurped the throne. “He did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, as his fathers had done” (2 Kings 14:29; 15:8-12). In him the dynasty of Jehu came to an end.

name: Zacharias
summary: The son or grandson of Jehoiada, the high priest in the times of Ahaziah and Joash. After the death of Jehoiada he boldly condemned both the king and the people for their rebellion against God (2 Chr. 24:20), which so stirred up their resentment against him that at the king’s commandment they stoned him with stones, and he died “in the court of the house of the Lord” (24:21). Christ alludes to this deed of murder in Matt. 23:35, Luke 11:51.

name: Zattu
summary: Id., one whose descendants returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:8; Neh. 7:13); probably the same as Zatthu.

name: Zeeb
summary: The wolf, one of the two leaders of the great Midianite host which invaded Israel and was utterly routed by Gideon. The division of that host, which attempted to escape across the Jordan, under Oreb and Zeeb, was overtaken by the Ephraimites, who, in a great battle, completely vanquished them, their leaders being taken and slain (Judg. 7:25; Ps. 83:11; Isa. 10:26).

name: Zeresh
summary: Star of Venus, the wife of Haman, whom she instigated to prepare a gallows for Mordecai (Esther 5:10).

name: Zillah
summary: Shadow, one of the wives of Lamech, of the line of Cain, and mother of Tubal-cain (Gen. 4:19, 22).

name: Zipporah
summary: A female bird. Reuel’s daughter, who became the wife of Moses (Ex. 2:21). In consequence of the event recorded in Ex. 4:24-26, she and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer, when so far on the way with Moses toward Egypt, were sent back by him to her own kinsfolk, the Midianites, with whom they sojourned till Moses afterwards joined them (18:2-6).

name: Zuph
summary: Honeycomb, a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Elkanah and Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1); called also Zophai (1 Chr. 6:26).

name: Abdon
summary: The son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:13-15). He is probably the Bedan of 1 Sam. 12:11.

name: Abdon
summary: The first-born of Gibeon of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

name: Abiah
summary: The second son of Samuel (1 Sam. 8:2; 1 Chr. 6:28). His conduct, along with that of his brother, as a judge in Beer-sheba, to which office his father had appointed him, led to popular discontent, and ultimately provoked the people to demand a royal form of government.

name: Abida
summary: Or Abi’dah, father of knowledge; knowing, one of the five sons of Midian, who was the son of Abraham by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:33), and apparently the chief of an Arab tribe.

name: Abihail
summary: The father of Esther and uncle of Mordecai (Esther 2:15).

name: Abijah
summary: The daughter of Zechariah (2 Chr. 29:1; comp. Isa. 8:2), and afterwards the wife of Ahaz. She is also called Abi (2 Kings 18:2).

name: Abijah
summary: A descendant of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, a chief of one of the twenty-four orders into which the priesthood was divided by David (1 Chr. 24:10). The order of Abijah was one of those which did not return from the Captivity (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42; 12:1).

name: Abimael
summary: Father of Mael, one of the sons or descendants of Joktan, in Northern Arabia (Gen. 10:28; 1 Chr. 1:22).

name: Abishur
summary: Father of the wall; i.e., “mason”, one of the two sons of Shammai of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 29).

name: Abital
summary: Father of dew; i.e., “fresh”, David’s fifth wife (2 Sam. 3:4).

name: Adaiah
summary: Timely (1 Chr. 6:21). A Gershonite Levite.

name: Adbeel
summary: Miracle of God, the third of the twelve sons of Ishmael, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:13; 1 Chr. 1:29).

name: Adrammelech
summary: A son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria (2 Kings 19:37; Isa. 37:38).

name: Adriel
summary: Flock of God, the son of Barzillai, the Meholathite, to whom Saul gave in marriage his daughter Merab (1 Sam. 18:19). The five sons that sprang from this union were put to death by the Gibeonites (2 Sam. 21:8, 9. Here it is said that Michal “brought up” [R.V., “bare”] these five sons, either that she treated them as if she had been their own mother, or that for “Michal” we should read “Merab,” as in 1 Sam. 18:19).

name: Agabus
summary: A “prophet,” probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He prophesied at Antioch of an approaching famine (Acts 11:27, 28). Many years afterwards he met Paul at Caesarea, and warned him of the bonds and affliction that awaited him at Jerusalem should he persist in going thither (Acts 21:10-12).

name: Ahab
summary: A false prophet referred to by Jeremiah (Jer. 29:21), of whom nothing further is known.

name: Ahiam
summary: Mother’s brother, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:33; 1 Chr. 11:35).

name: Ahio
summary: One of the sons of Jehiel the Gibeonite (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:37).

name: Akan
summary: He twists, one of the sons of Ezer, the son of Seir the Horite (1 Chr. 1:42).

name: Alemeth
summary: One of the sons of Jehoadah, or Jarah, son of Ahaz (1 Chr. 8:36).

name: Alexander
summary: A coppersmith who, with Hymenaeus and others, promulgated certain heresies regarding the resurrection (1 Tim. 1:19; 2 Tim. 4:14), and made shipwreck of faith and of a good conscience. Paul excommunicated him (1 Tim. 1:20; comp. 1 Cor. 5:5).

name: Allon
summary: The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Almodad
summary: Immeasurable, the first named of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:26), the founder of an Arabian tribe.

name: Amariah
summary: One of the descendants of Aaron by Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:7, 52). He was probably the last of the high priests of Eleazar’s line prior to the transfer of that office to Eli, of the line of Ithamar.

name: Amariah
summary: A Levite, son of Hebron, of the lineage of Moses (1 Chr. 23:19; 24:23).

name: Amasai
summary: A Levite, son of Elkanah, of the ancestry of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:25, 35).

name: Amittai
summary: True, the father of Jonah the prophet, a native of Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25; Jonah 1:1).

name: Amminadab
summary: Chief of the 112 descendants of Uzziel the Levite (1 Chr. 15:10, 11).

name: Amon
summary: The governor of Samaria in the time of Ahab. The prophet Micaiah was committed to his custody (1 Kings 22:26; 2 Chr. 18:25).

name: Amraphel
summary: King of Shinar, southern Chaldea, one of the confederates of Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, in a war against Sodom and cities of the plain (Gen. 14:1, 4). It is now found that Amraphel (or Ammirapaltu) is the Khammu-rabi whose name appears on recently-discovered monuments. After defeating Arioch (q.v.) he united Babylonia under one rule, and made Babylon his capital.

name: Anamim
summary: The name of an Egyptian tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11).

name: Ananias (High Priest)
summary: The high priest before whom Paul was brought in the procuratorship of Felix (Acts 23:2, 5, 24). He was so enraged at Paul’s noble declaration, “I have lived in all good conscience before God until this day,” that he commanded one of his attendants to smite him on the mouth. Smarting under this unprovoked insult, Paul quickly replied, “God shall smite thee, thou whited wall.” Being reminded that Ananias was the high priest, to whose office all respect was to be paid, he answered, “I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest” (Acts 23:5). This expression has occasioned some difficulty, as it is scarcely probable that Paul should have been ignorant of so public a fact. The expression may…

name: Anath
summary: An answer; i.e., to “prayer”, the father of Shamgar, who was one of the judges of Israel (Judg. 3:31).

name: Aner
summary: A Canaanitish chief who joined his forces with those of Abraham in pursuit of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

name: Aran
summary: Wild goat, a descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:28).

name: Archippus
summary: Master of the horse, a “fellow-soldier” of Paul’s (Philemon 1:2), whom he exhorts to renewed activity (Col. 4:17). He was a member of Philemon’s family, probably his son.

name: Arioch (king of Ellasar)
summary: A king of Ellasar who was confederate with Chedorlamer (Gen. 14:1, 9). The tablets recently discovered by Mr. Pinches (see CHALDEA) show the true reading is Eri-Aku of Larsa. This Elamite name meant “servant of the moon-god.” It was afterwards changed into Rimsin, “Have mercy, O moon-god.”

name: Arkite
summary: (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15), a designation of certain descendants from the Phoenicians or Sidonians, the inhabitants of Arka, 12 miles north of Tripoli, opposite the northern extremity of Lebanon.

name: Ater
summary: Ezra 2:16.

name: Ater
summary: Ezra 2:42.

name: Azareel
summary: A priest (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Azariah
summary: High priest in the reign of Uzziah, king of Judah (2 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 26:17-20). He was contemporary with the prophets Isaiah, Amos, and Joel.

name: Azmaveth
summary: One of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:31).

name: Azubah
summary: The daughter of Shilhi, and mother of king Jehoshaphat (1 Kings 22:42).

name: Azubah
summary: The wife of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:18, 19).

name: Baal
summary: A Benjamite, son of Jehiel, the progenitor of the Gibeonites (1 Chr. 8:30; 9:36).

name: Baanah
summary: The father of Heled, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29; 1 Chr. 11:30).

name: Baladan
summary: He has given a son, the father of the Babylonian king (2 Kings 20:12; Isa. 39:1) Merodach-baladan (q.v.).

name: Barachel
summary: Whom God has blessed, a Buzite, the father of Elihu, one of Job’s friends (Job 32:2, 6).

name: Barkos
summary: Painter, (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55). The father of some of the Nethinim.

name: Barzillai
summary: A priest who married a daughter of the preceding (Ezra 2:61).

name: Ben-ammi
summary: Son of my kindred; i.e., “born of incest”, the son of Lot by his youngest daughter (Gen. 19:38).

name: Beor
summary: The father of Bela, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:32).

name: Beriah
summary: A Benjamite who with his brother Shema founded Ajalon and expelled the Gittites (1 Chr. 8:13).

name: Bigthana
summary: One of the eunuchs who “kept the door” in the court of Ahasuerus. With Teresh he conspired against the king’s life. Mordecai detected the conspiracy, and the culprits were hanged (Esther 2:21-23; 6:1-3).

name: Bilshan
summary: Son of the tongue; i.e., “eloquent”, a man of some note who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7).

name: Casluhim
summary: Fortified, a people descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:14; 1 Chr. 1:12). Their original seat was probably somewhere in Lower Egypt, along the sea-coast to the south border of Palestine.

name: Chenaniah
summary: Whom Jehovah hath made. “Chief of the Levites,” probably a Kohathite (1 Chr. 15:22), and therefore not the same as mentioned in 26:29.

name: Chushan-rishathaim
summary: Cush of double wickedness, or governor of two presidencies, the king of Mesopotamia who oppressed Israel in the generation immediately following Joshua (Judg. 3:8). We learn from the Tell-el-Amarna tablets that Palestine had been invaded by the forces of Aram-naharaim (A.V., “Mesopotamia”) more than once, long before the Exodus, and that at the time they were written the king of Aram-naharaim was still intriguing in Canaan. It is mentioned among the countries which took part in the attack upon Egypt in the reign of Rameses III. (of the Twentieth Dynasty), but as its king is not one of the princes stated to have been conquered by the Pharaoh, it would seem that he did not actually enter…

name: Claudius (4th Roman Emperor)
summary: The fourth Roman emperor. He succeeded Caligula (A.D. 41). Though in general he treated the Jews, especially those in Asia and Egypt, with great indulgence, yet about the middle of his reign (A.D. 49) he banished them all from Rome (Acts 18:2). In this edict the Christians were included, as being, as was supposed, a sect of Jews. The Jews, however soon again returned to Rome. During the reign of this emperor, several persecutions of the Christians by the Jews took place in the dominions of Herod Agrippa, in one of which the apostle James was “killed” (12:2). He died A.D. 54.

name: Cleophas
summary: (abbreviation of Cleopatros), one of the two disciples with whom Jesus conversed on the way to Emmaus on the day of the resurrection (Luke 24:18). We know nothing definitely regarding him. It is not certain that he was the Clopas of John 19:25, or the Alphaeus of Matt. 10:3, although he may have been so.

name: Crispus
summary: Curled, the chief of the synagogue at Corinth (Acts 18:8). He was converted and, with his family, baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14).

name: Daniel
summary: David’s second son, “born unto him in Hebron, of Abigail the Carmelitess” (1 Chr. 3:1). He is called also Chileab (2 Sam. 3:3).

name: Dedan (son of Raamah)
summary: A son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7). His descendants are mentioned in Isa. 21:13, and Ezek. 27:15. They probably settled among the sons of Cush, on the north-west coast of the Persian Gulf.

name: Dedan (son of Jokshan)
summary: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

name: Delaiah
summary: The head of one of the bands of exiles that returned under Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:60; Neh. 7:62).

name: Delaiah
summary: A son of Shemaiah, and one of the courtiers to whom Jeremiah’s first roll of prophecy was read (Jer. 36:12).

name: Dodanim
summary: Leaders, a race descended from Javan (Gen. 10:4). They are known in profane history as the Dardani, originally inhabiting Illyricum. They were a semi-Pelasgic race, and in the ethnographical table (Gen. 10) they are grouped with the Chittim (q.v.). In 1 Chr. 1:7, they are called Rodanim. The LXX. and the Samaritan Version also read Rhodii, whence some have concluded that the Rhodians, the inhabitants of the island of Rhodes, are meant.

name: Dodo
summary: A Bethlehemite, and father of Elhanan, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:24).

name: Ebal (son of Shobal)
summary: A descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:23).

name: Ebal (son of Joktan)
summary: A descendant of Eber (1 Chr. 1:22), called also Obal (Gen. 10:28).

name: Eder
summary: The second of the three sons of Mushi, of the family of Merari, appointed to the Levitical office (1 Chr. 23:23; 24:30).

name: Eglah
summary: A heifer, one of David’s wives, and mother of Ithream (2 Sam. 3:5; 1 Chr. 3:3). According to a Jewish tradition she was Michal.

name: Elah
summary: One of the Edomite chiefs or “dukes” of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:41).

name: Elam (son of Shem)
summary: Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles. The name Elam is an Assyrian word meaning “high.” “The inhabitants of Elam, or ‘the Highlands,’ to the east of Babylon, were called Elamites. They were divided into several branches, speaking different dialects of the same agglutinative language. The race to which they belonged was brachycephalic, or short-headed, like the pre-Semitic Sumerians of Babylonia. “The earliest Elamite kingdom seems to have been that of Anzan, the exact…

name: Eldad
summary: Whom God has loved, one of the seventy elders whom Moses appointed (Num. 11:26, 27) to administer justice among the people. He, with Medad, prophesied in the camp instead of going with the rest to the tabernacle, as Moses had commanded. This incident was announced to Moses by Joshua, who thought their conduct in this respect irregular. Moses replied, “Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the Lord’s people were prophets” (Num. 11:24-30; comp. Mark 9:38; Luke 9:49).

name: Eleasah
summary: One of the descendants of Judah, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:39, “Eleasah”).

name: Eleazar
summary: The son of Dodo the Ahohite, of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the three most eminent of David’s thirty-seven heroes (1 Chr. 11:12) who broke through the Philistine host and brought him water from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:9, 16).

name: Elhanan
summary: A warrior of the time of David famed for his exploits. In the Authorized Version (2 Sam. 21:19) it is recorded that “Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath.” The Revised Version here rightly omits the words “the brother of.” They were introduced in the Authorized Version to bring this passage into agreement with 1 Chr. 20:5, where it is said that he “slew Lahmi the brother of Goliath.” Goliath the Gittite was killed by David (1 Sam. 17). The exploit of Elhanan took place late in David’s reign.

name: Elhanan
summary: The son of Dodo, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:24).

name: Eliam
summary: The father of Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah (2 Sam. 11:3). In 1 Chr. 3:5 his name is Ammiel.

name: Eliathah
summary: To whom God will come, one of the foureen sons of the Levite Heman, and musician of the temple in the time of David (1 Chr. 25:4).

name: Elipheleh
summary: God will distinguish him, one of the porters appointed to play “on the Sheminith” on the occasion of the bringing up of the ark to the city of David (1 Chr. 15:18, 21).

name: Elishah
summary: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis. This may be meant by “the isles of Elishah” (Ezek. 27:7).

name: Elishama
summary: One of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16).

name: Elkanah
summary: The second son of Korah (Ex. 6:24), or, according to 1 Chr. 6:22, 23, more correctly his grandson.

name: Elon
summary: A Hittite, father of Bashemath, Esau’s wife (Gen. 26:34).

name: Elon
summary: One of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

name: Elon
summary: The eleventh of the Hebrew judges. He held office for ten years (Judg. 12:11, 12). He is called the Zebulonite.

name: Elymas
summary: Magician or sorcerer, the Arabic name of the Jew Bar-jesus, who withstood Paul and Barnabas in Cyprus. He was miraculously struck with blindness (Acts 13:11).

name: Enoch (son of Cain)
summary: The eldest son of Cain (Gen. 4:17), who built a city east of Eden in the land of Nod, and called it “after the name of his son Enoch.” This is the first “city” mentioned in Scripture.

name: Epher
summary: One of the sons of Midian, who was Abraham’s son by Keturah (Gen. 25:4).

name: Eshcol
summary: A young Amoritish chief who joined Abraham in the recovery of Lot from the hands of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

name: Ethan
summary: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 6:21), probably the same as Ethan (42).

name: Evil-merodach
summary: Merodach’s man, the son and successor of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:27; Jer. 52:31, 34). He seems to have reigned but two years (B.C. 562-560). Influenced probably by Daniel, he showed kindness to Jehoiachin, who had been a prisoner in Babylon for thirty-seven years. He released him, and “spoke kindly to him.” He was murdered by Nergal-sharezer=Neriglissar, his brother-in-law, who succeeded him (Jer. 39:3, 13).

name: Ezekiel
summary: One of the great prophets, the son of Buzi the priest (Ezek. 1:3). He was one of the Jewish exiles who settled at Tel-Abib, on the banks of the Chebar, “in the land of the Chaldeans.” He was probably carried away captive with Jehoiachin (1:2; 2 Kings 24:14-16) about B.C. 597. His prophetic call came to him “in the fifth year of Jehoiachin’s captivity” (B.C. 594). He had a house in the place of his exile, where he lost his wife, in the ninth year of his exile, by some sudden and unforeseen stroke (Ezek. 8:1; 24:18). He held a prominent place among the exiles, and was frequently consulted by the elders (8:1; 11:25; 14:1; 20:1). His ministry extended over twenty-three years (29:17), B.C.…

name: Gahar
summary: Lurking-place, one of the chief of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:47).

name: Gaius
summary: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14). During a heathen outbreak against Paul at Ephesus the mob seized Gaius and Aristarchus because they could not find Paul, and rushed with them into the theatre. Some have identified this Gaius with No. (2).

name: Gamaliel
summary: The son of rabbi Simeon, and grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel. He was a Pharisse, and therefore the opponent of the party of the Sadducees. He was noted for his learning, and was president of the Sanhedrim during the regins of Tiberius, Caligula, and Claudius, and died, it is said, about eighteen years before the destruction of Jerusalem. When the apostles were brought before the council, charged with preaching the resurrection of Jesus, as a zealous Pharisee Gamaliel councelled moderation and calmness. By a reference to well-known events, he advised them to “refrain from these men.” If their work or counsel was of man, it would come to nothing; but if it was of God, they could not…

name: Gedaliah
summary: the son of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 9).

name: Girgasite
summary: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan (Gen. 10:16), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites (Gen. 15:21; Deut. 7:1). They were a branch of the great family of the Hivites. Of their geographical position nothing is certainly known. Probably they lived somewhere in the central part of Western Palestine.

name: Hadar
summary: A son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15); in 1 Chr. 1:30 written Hadad.

name: Hadoram
summary: The fifth son of Joktan, the founder of an Arab tribe (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21).

name: Hammelech
summary: The king’s, the father of Jerahmeel, mentioned in Jer. 36:26. Some take this word as a common noun, “the king”, and understand that Jerahmeel was Jehoiakim’s son. Probably, however, it is to be taken as a proper name.

name: Hanan
summary: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

name: Hanan
summary: One of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:46).

name: Hanan
summary: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra (Neh. 8:7).

name: Hanani
summary: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 25).

name: Hanani
summary: Probably a brother of Nehemiah (Neh. 1:2; 7:2), who reported to him the melancholy condition of Jerusalem. Nehemiah afterwards appointed him to have charge of the city gates.

name: Hananiah
summary: Son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19, 21).

name: Hananiah
summary: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 23).

name: Harhur
summary: Fever, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:51).

name: Harsha
summary: Worker or enchanter, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:52; Neh. 7:54).

name: Hasrah
summary: Poverty, “keeper of the wardrobe,” i.e., of the sacerdotal vestments (2 Chr. 34:22); called Harhas 2 Kings 22:14. He was husband of the prophetess Huldah.

name: Hasshub
summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (Neh. 11:15; 1 Chr. 9:14).

name: Hasupha
summary: Uncovered, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

name: Hatipha
summary: Captured, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:54).

name: Hatita
summary: Exploration, one of the temple porters or janitors (Ezra 2:42). He returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel.

name: Hattush
summary: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:2).

name: Havilah (son of Cush)
summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

name: Havilah (son of Joktan)
summary: A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:29; 1 Chr. 1:23).

name: Hazarmaveth
summary: Court of death, the third son of Joktan, and a region in Arabia-Felix settled by him (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20). It is probably the modern province of Hadramaut, situated on the Indian Ocean east of the modern Yemen.

name: Helah
summary: Rust, (1 Chr. 4:5, 7), one of the wives of Ashur.

name: Helek
summary: A portion, (Josh. 17:2), descended from Manasseh.

name: Helem
summary: Zech. 6:10, one who returned from Babylon.

name: Henadad
summary: Favour of Hadad, the name of a Levite after the Captivity (Ezra 3:9).

name: Hezrai
summary: A Carmelite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:37).

name: Hillel
summary: Praising, a Pirathonite, father of the judge Abdon (Judg. 12:13, 15).

name: Hobab
summary: Beloved, the Kenite, has been usually identified with Jethro (q.v.), Ex. 18:5, 27; comp. Num. 10:29, 30. In Judg. 4:11, the word rendered “father-in-law” means properly any male relative by marriage (comp. Gen. 19:14, “son-in-law,” A.V.), and should be rendered “brother-in-law,” as in the R.V. His descendants followed Israel to Canaan (Num. 10:29), and at first pitched their tents near Jericho, but afterwards settled in the south in the borders of Arad (Judg. 1:8-11, 16).

name: Hotham
summary: A stroke, great-grandson of Asher (1 Chr. 7:35).

name: Hul
summary: Circle, the second son of Aram (Gen. 10:23), and grandson of Shem.

name: Huldah
summary: Weasel, a prophetess; the wife of Shallum. She was consulted regarding the “book of the law” discovered by the high priest Hilkiah (2 Kings 22:14-20; 2 Chr. 34:22-28). She resided in that part of Jerusalem called the Mishneh (A.V., “the college;” R.V., “the second quarter”), supposed by some to be the suburb between the inner and the outer wall, the second or lower city, Akra. Miriam (Ex. 15:20) and Deborah (Judg. 4:4) are the only others who bear the title of “prophetess,” for the word in Isa. 8:3 means only the prophet’s wife.

name: Hur
summary: One of the five princes of Midian who were defeated and slain by the Israelites under the command of Phinehas (Num. 31:8).

name: Hurai
summary: Linen-worker, one of David’s heroes, a native of the valley of Mount Gaash (1 Chr. 11:32).

name: Ibzan
summary: Illustrious, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:8-10). He ruled seven years.

name: Ilai
summary: An Ahohite, one of David’s chief warriors (1 Chr. 11:29); called also Zalmon (2 Sam. 23:28).

name: Ira
summary: An Ithrite, also one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:38).

name: Iram
summary: Citizen, chief of an Edomite tribe in Mount Seir (Gen. 36:43).

name: Ishbak
summary: Leaving, one of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

name: Ittai
summary: A Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29).

name: Jaala
summary: A wild she-goat, one of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned from the Captivity (Neh. 7:58).

name: Jaaziah
summary: Comforted by Jehovah, a descendant of Merari the Levite (1 Chr. 24:26, 27).

name: Jaaziel
summary: Comforted by God, a Levitical musician (1 Chr. 15:18).

name: Jabez
summary: A descendant of Judah, of whom it is recorded that “God granted him that which he requested” (1 Chr. 4:9, 10).

name: Jachin
summary: One of the priests who returned from the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

name: Jaddua
summary: The last high priest mentioned in the Old Testament (Neh. 12:11, 22), sons of Jonathan.

name: Jahath
summary: A son of Shimei, and grandson of Gershom (1 Chr. 23:10).

name: Jahaziel
summary: The third son of Hebron (1 Chr. 23:19).

name: Jair
summary: The father of Elhanan, who slew Lahmi, the brother of Goliath (1 Chr. 20:5).

name: Jairus
summary: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum, whose only daughter Jesus restored to life (Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41). Entering into the chamber of death, accompanied by Peter and James and John and the father and mother of the maiden, he went forward to the bed whereon the corpse lay, and said, Talitha cumi, i.e., “Maid, arise,” and immediately the spirit of the maiden came to her again, and she arose straightway; and “at once to strengthen that life which had come back to her, and to prove that she was indeed no ghost, but had returned to the realities of a mortal existence, he commanded to give her something to eat” (Mark 5:43).

name: Jasher
summary: Upright. “The Book of Jasher,” rendered in the LXX. “the Book of the Upright One,” by the Vulgate “the Book of Just Ones,” was probably a kind of national sacred song-book, a collection of songs in praise of the heroes of Israel, a “book of golden deeds,” a national anthology. We have only two specimens from the book, (1) the words of Joshua which he spake to the Lord at the crisis of the battle of Beth-horon (Josh. 10:12, 13); and (2) “the Song of the Bow,” that beautiful and touching mournful elegy which David composed on the occasion of the death of Saul and Jonathan (2 Sam. 1:18-27).

name: Jashobeam
summary: Dweller among the people; or to whom the people turn, the Hachmonite (1 Chr. 11:11), one of David’s chief heroes who joined him at Ziklag (12:6). He was the first of the three who broke through the host of the Philistines to fetch water to David from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:13-17). He is also called Adino the Eznite (8).

name: Jebusite
summary: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.). At the time of the arrival of the Israelites in Palestine they were ruled by Adonizedek (Josh. 10:1, 23). They were defeated by Joshua, and their king was slain; but they were not entirely driven out of Jebus till the time of David, who made it the capital of his kingdom instead of Hebron. The site on which the temple was afterwards built belonged to Araunah, a Jebusite, from whom it was purchased by David, who refused to accept it as a free gift (2 Sam. 24:16-25; 1 Chr. 21:24, 25).

name: Jecoliah
summary: Able through Jehovah, the wife of King Amaziah, and mother of King Uzziah (2 Chr. 26:3).

name: Jehoaddan
summary: Jehovah his ornament, the wife of King Jehoash, and mother of King Amaziah (2 Kings 14:2).

name: Jehoshabeath
summary: Jehovah-swearing, the daughter of Jehoram, the king of Israel. She is called Jehoshabeath in 2 Chr. 22:11. She was the only princess of the royal house who was married to a high priest, Jehoiada (2 Chr. 22:11).

name: Jehoshaphat
summary: The son of Nimshi, and father of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 9:2, 14).

name: Jehozabad
summary: The son of Shomer, one of the two conspirators who put king Jehoash to death in Millo in Jerusalem (2 Kings 12:21).

name: Jeremoth
summary: 1 Chr. 24:30, a Merarite Levite.

name: Jerimoth
summary: A Levitical musician under Heman his father (1 Chr. 25:4).

name: Jeroham
summary: 1 Chr. 9:12; a priest, perhaps the same as in Neh. 11:12.

name: Jerushah
summary: Possession, or possessed; i.e., “by a husband”, the wife of Uzziah, and mother of king Jotham (2 Kings 15:33).

name: Jeshaiah
summary: A Kohathite Levite, the father of Joram, of the family of Eliezer (1 Chr. 26:25); called also Isshiah (24:21).

name: Jeshaiah
summary: One of the sons of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 15).

name: Jesharelah
summary: Upright towards God, the head of the seventh division of Levitical musicians (1 Chr. 25:14).

name: Jeshua
summary: Ezra 2:6; Neh. 7:11.

name: Jetheth
summary: A peg, or a prince, one of the Edomitish kings of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:40).

name: Jetur
summary: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

name: Jeush
summary: A Levite, one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chr. 23:10, 11).

name: Joab
summary: Ezra 2:6.

name: Joanna
summary: The wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 8:3). She was one of the women who ministered to our Lord, and to whom he appeared after his resurrection (Luke 8:3; 24:10).

name: Joash
summary: One of King Ahab’s sons (1 Kings 22:26).

name: Jobab (son of Joktan)
summary: One of the sons of Joktan, and founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 10:29).

name: Jochebed
summary: Jehovah is her glory, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Miriam, Aaron, and Moses (Num. 26:59). She is spoken of as the sister of Kohath, Amram’s father (Ex. 6:20; comp. 16, 18; 2:1-10).

name: Joel
summary: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 15:7, 11).

name: Joel
summary: The second of the twelve minor prophets. He was the son of Pethuel. His personal history is only known from his book.

name: Joram
summary: The son of Tou, king of Hamath, sent by his father to congratulate David on his victory over Hadarezer, king of Syria (1 Chr. 18:10; called Joram 2 Sam. 8:10).

name: Joseph (son of Asaph)
summary: One of the sons of Asaph, head of the first division of sacred musicians (1 Chr. 25:2, 9).

name: Jucal
summary: Able, the son of Shelemiah. He is also called Jucal (Jer. 38:1). He was one of the two persons whom Zedekiah sent to request the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the kingdom (Jer. 37:3) during the time of its final siege by Nebuchadnezzar. He was accompanied by Zephaniah (q.v.).

name: Julius
summary: The centurion of the Augustan cohort, or the emperor’s body-guard, in whose charge Paul was sent prisoner to Rome (Acts 27:1, 3, 43). He entreated Paul “courteously,” showing in many ways a friendly regard for him.

name: Kedemah
summary: Eastward, the last-named of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

name: Kelita
summary: Dwarf, a Levite who assisted Ezra in expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:7; 10:10).

name: Laish
summary: The father of Phalti (1 Sam. 25:44).

name: Lemuel
summary: Dedicated to God, a king whom his mother instructed (Prov. 31:1-9). Nothing is certainly known concerning him. The rabbis identified him with Solomon.

name: Lo-ruhamah
summary: Not pitied, the name of the prophet Hosea’s first daughter, a type of Jehovah’s temporary rejection of his people (Hos. 1:6; 2:23).

name: Lucius
summary: Of Cyrene, a Christian teacher at Antioch (Acts 13:1), and Paul’s kinsman (Rom. 16:21). His name is Latin, but his birthplace seems to indicate that he was one of the Jews of Cyrene, in North Africa.

name: Lud
summary: The fourth son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17), ancestor of the Lydians probably.

name: Ludim
summary: Probably the same as Lud (2) (comp. Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11). They are associated (Jer. 46:9) with African nations as mercenaries of the king of Egypt.

name: Maacah
summary: A daughter of Talmai, king of the old native population of Geshur. She became one of David’s wives, and was the mother of Absalom (2 Sam. 3:3).

name: Maachah
summary: The father of Achish, the king of Gath (1 Kings 2:39), called also Maoch (1 Sam. 27:2).

name: Maaseiah
summary: One of the Levites whom David appointed as porter for the ark (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Maasiai
summary: Work of Jehovah, one of the priests resident at Jerusalem at the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Madai
summary: Middle land, the third “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the name by which the Medes are known on the Assyrian monuments.

name: Mahath
summary: A Kohathite Levite, father of Elkanah (1 Chr. 6:35).

name: Mahazioth
summary: Visions, a Kohathite Levite, chief of the twenty-third course of musicians (1 Chr. 25:4, 30).

name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
summary: Plunder speedeth; spoil hasteth, (Isa. 8:1-3; comp. Zeph. 1:14), a name Isaiah was commanded first to write in large characters on a tablet, and afterwards to give as a symbolical name to a son that was to be born to him (Isa. 8:1, 3), as denoting the sudden attack on Damascus and Syria by the Assyrian army.

name: Malcham
summary: (2 Sam. 12:30, Heb., R.V., “their king;” Jer. 49:1, 3, R.V.; Zeph. 1:5), the national idol of the Ammonites. When Rabbah was taken by David, the crown of this idol was among the spoils. The weight is said to have been “a talent of gold” (above 100 lbs.). The expression probably denotes its value rather than its weight. It was adorned with precious stones.

name: Mallothi
summary: My fulness, a Kohathite Levite, one of the sons of Heman the Levite (1 Chr. 25:4), and chief of the nineteenth division of the temple musicians (26).

name: Mash
summary: (= Meshech 1 Chr. 1:17), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him (Gen. 10:23) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia. Some have supposed that they were the inhabitants of Mount Masius, the present Karja Baghlar, which forms part of the chain of Taurus.

name: Massa
summary: A lifting up, gift, one of the sons of Ishmael, the founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:14); a nomad tribe inhabiting the Arabian desert toward Babylonia.

name: Mattan
summary: A priest of Baal, slain before his altar during the reformation under Jehoiada (2 Kings 11:18).

name: Mattaniah
summary: A Levite, son of Heman, the chief of the ninth class of temple singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 16).

name: Matthias
summary: Gift of God. Acts 1:23.

name: Medan
summary: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

name: Mehetabel
summary: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:39).

name: Mehunim
summary: Habitations, (2 Chr. 26:7; R.V. “Meunim,” Vulg. Ammonitae), a people against whom Uzziah waged a successful war. This word is in Hebrew the plural of Ma’on, and thus denotes the Maonites who inhabited the country on the eastern side of the Wady el-Arabah. They are again mentioned in 1 Chr. 4:41 (R.V.), in the reign of King Hezekiah, as a Hamite people, settled in the eastern end of the valley of Gedor, in the wilderness south of Palestine. In this passage the Authorized Version has “habitation,” erroneously following the translation of Luther. They are mentioned in the list of those from whom the Nethinim were made up (Ezra 2:50; Neh. 7:52).

name: Melech
summary: King, the second of Micah’s four sons (1 Chr. 8:35), and thus grandson of Mephibosheth.

name: Melzar
summary: Probably a Persian word meaning master of wine, i.e., chief butler; the title of an officer at the Babylonian court (Dan. 1:11, 16) who had charge of the diet of the Hebrew youths.

name: Mered
summary: Rebellion, one of the sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

name: Meshillemith
summary: A priest, the son of Immer (Neh. 11:13).

name: Meshullam
summary: A priest (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Mezahab
summary: Water of gold, the father of Matred (Gen. 36:39; 1 Chr. 1:50), and grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom.

name: Mibsam
summary: One of Ishmael’s twelve sons, and head of an Arab tribe (Gen. 25:13).

name: Mibzar
summary: Fortress, one of the Edomitish “dukes” descended from Esau (Gen. 36:42; 1 Chr. 1:53).

name: Micah
summary: “The Morasthite,” so called to distinguish him from Micaiah, the son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He was a prophet of Judah, a contemporary of Isaiah (Micah 1:1), a native of Moresheth of Gath (1:14, 15). Very little is known of the circumstances of his life (comp. Jer. 26:18, 19).

name: Micha
summary: The son of Zabdi, a Levite of the family of Asaph (Neh. 11:17, 22).

name: Michaiah
summary: A Levite (Neh. 12:35).

name: Michaiah
summary: 2 Kings 22:12.

name: Michaiah
summary: The son of Gemariah. He reported to the king’s officers Jeremiah’s prediction, which he had heard Baruch read (Jer. 36:11, 13) from his father Gemariah’s chamber in the temple.

name: Mishael
summary: A Levite; the eldest of the three sons of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

name: Mishma
summary: One of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:14), and founder of an Arab tribe.

name: Mishma
summary: A Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:25, 26).

name: Mispereth
summary: Number, one of the Jews who accompanied Zerubbabel from Babylon (Ezra 2:2); called also Mispereth (Neh. 7:7).

name: Naarah
summary: A girl, the second of Ashur’s two wives, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:5, 6).

name: Nadab
summary: One of the sons of Shammai in the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 30).

name: Naharai
summary: Snorer, a Berothite, one of David’s heroes, and armour-bearer of Joab (1 Chr. 11:39).

name: Naphtuhim
summary: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan. This city was the royal residence, it is said, of Queen Candace (Acts 8:27). Here there are extensive and splendid ruins.

name: Nehemiah
summary: Ezra 2:2; Neh. 7:7.

name: Nergal-sharezer
summary: Another of the “princes,” who bore the title of “Rabmag.” He was one of those who were sent to release Jeremiah from prison (Jer. 39:13) by “the captain of the guard.” He was a Babylonian grandee of high rank. From profane history and the inscriptions, we are led to conclude that he was the Neriglissar who murdered Evil-merodach, the son of Nebuchadnezzar, and succeeded him on the throne of Babylon (B.C. 559-556). He was married to a daughter of Nebuchadnezzar. The ruins of a palace, the only one on the right bank of the Euphrates, bear inscriptions denoting that it was built by this king. He was succeeded by his son, a mere boy, who was murdered after a reign of some nine months by a…

name: Neziah
summary: Victory; pure, Ezra 2:54; Neh. 7:56.

name: Nogah
summary: Splendour, one of David’s sons, born at Jerusalem (1 Chr. 3:7).

name: Obadiah
summary: A descendant of Saul (1 Chr. 8:38).

name: Ohad
summary: United, or power, the third son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10).

name: Onesimus
summary: Useful, a slave who, after robbing his master Philemon (q.v.) at Colosse, fled to Rome, where he was converted by the apostle Paul, who sent him back to his master with the epistle which bears his name. In it he beseeches Philemon to receive his slave as a “faithful and beloved brother.” Paul offers to pay to Philemon anything his slave had taken, and to bear the wrong he had done him. He was accompanied on his return by Tychicus, the bearer of the Epistle to the Colossians (Philemon 1:16, 18). The story of this fugitive Colossian slave is a remarkable evidence of the freedom of access to the prisoner which was granted to all, and “a beautiful illustration both of the character of St. Paul…

name: Onesiphorus
summary: Bringing profit, an Ephesian Christian who showed great kindness to Paul at Rome. He served him in many things, and had oft refreshed him. Paul expresses a warm interest in him and his household (2 Tim. 1:16-18; 4:19).

name: Ophir
summary: One of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:29).

name: Orpah
summary: Forelock or fawn, a Moabitess, the wife of Chilion (Ruth 1:4; 4:10). On the death of her husband she accompanied Naomi, her mother-in-law, part of the way to Bethlehem, and then returned to Moab.

name: Ozni
summary: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon (Gen. 46:16; Num. 26:16).

name: Pedaiah
summary: The father of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:17-19).

name: Pelaiah
summary: A Levite who expounded the law (Neh. 8:7).

name: Pelatiah
summary: One of the twenty-five princes of the people against whom Ezekiel prophesied on account of their wicked counsel (Ezek. 11:1-13).

name: Perida
summary: One whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:55); called also Perida (Neh. 7:57).

name: Phaltiel
summary: Deliverance of the Lord, the son of Laish of Gallim (1 Sam. 25:44)= Phaltiel (2 Sam. 3:15). Michal, David’s wife, was given to him.

name: Potiphar
summary: Dedicated to Ra; i.e., to the sun-god, the Egyptian to whom the Ishmaelites sold Joseph (Gen. 39:1). He was “captain of the guard”, i.e., chief, probably, of the state police, who, while they formed part of the Egyptian army, were also largely employed in civil duties (37:36; marg., “chief of the executioners”). Joseph, though a foreigner, gradually gained his confidence, and became overseer over all his possessions. Believing the false accusation which his profligate wife brought against Joseph, Potiphar cast him into prison, where he remained for some years.

name: Publius
summary: “the chief man of the island” of Malta (Acts 28:7), who courteously entertained Paul and his shipwrecked companions for three days, till they found a more permanent place of residence; for they remained on the island for three months, till the stormy season had passed. The word here rendered “chief man” (protos) is supposed by some to be properly a Maltese term, the official title of the governor.

name: Raamah
summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

name: Ram
summary: One of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25, 27).

name: Rapha
summary: A Benjamite, the son of Binea (1 Chr. 8:2, 37), a descendant of Saul.

name: Reba
summary: Fourth, one of the Midianite chiefs slain by the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 31:8; Josh. 13:21).

name: Reelaiah
summary: Thunder of the Lord, one of the princes who returned from the Exile (Neh. 7:7); called also Reelaiah (Ezra 2:2).

name: Rehob
summary: The father of Hadadezer, king of Tobah (2 Sam. 8:3, 12).

name: Rekem
summary: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites destroyed (Num. 31:8).

name: Rekem
summary: One of the sons of Hebron (1 Chr. 2:43, 44).

name: Riphath
summary: A crusher, Gomer’s second son (Gen. 10:3), supposed to have been the ancestor of the Paphlagonians.

name: Romamti-ezer
summary: Elevation of help, one of the sons of Heman, “the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn.” He was head of the “four-and-twentieth” course of singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 31).

name: Sabtah
summary: Rest, the third son of Cush (Gen. 10:7; 1 Chr. 1:9).

name: Sabtecha
summary: The fifth son of Cush.

name: Sallu
summary: A priest (Neh. 12:7).

name: Salome
summary: The wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John (Mat. 27:56), and probably the sister of Mary, the mother of our Lord (John 19:25). She sought for her sons places of honour in Christ’s kingdom (Matt. 20:20, 21; comp. 19:28). She witnessed the crucifixion (Mark 15:40), and was present with the other women at the sepulchre (Matt. 27:56).

name: Seba
summary: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

name: Segub
summary: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:21, 22).

name: Seraiah
summary: The father of Joab (1 Chr. 4:13, 14).

name: Seraiah
summary: The son of Neriah. When Zedekiah made a journey to Babylon to do homage to Nebuchadnezzar, Seraiah had charge of the royal gifts to be presented on that occasion. Jeremiah took advantage of the occasion, and sent with Seraiah a word of cheer to the exiles in Babylon, and an announcement of the doom in store for that guilty city. The roll containing this message (Jer. 50:1-8) Seraiah was to read to the exiles, and then, after fixing a stone to it, was to throw it into the Euphrates, uttering, as it sank, the prayer recorded in Jer. 51:59-64. Babylon was at this time in the height of its glory, the greatest and most powerful monarchy in the world. Scarcely seventy years elapsed when the words…

name: Sered
summary: Fear, one of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

name: Shallum
summary: Keeper of the temple vestments in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:14).

name: Shallum
summary: One of the posterity of Judah (1 Chr. 2:40, 41).

name: Shamer
summary: A man of Asher (1 Chr. 7:32); called also Shamer (34).

name: Shamgar
summary: The Philistines from the maritime plain had made incursions into the Hebrew upland for the purposes of plunder, when one of this name, the son of Anath, otherwise unknown, headed a rising for the purpose of freeing the land from this oppression. He repelled the invasion, slaying 600 men with an “ox goad” (q.v.). The goad was a formidable sharpointed instrument, sometimes ten feet long. He was probably contemporary for a time with Deborah and Barak (Judg. 3:31; 5:6).

name: Shammah
summary: One of David’s mighties (2 Sam. 23:25); called also Shammoth (1 Chr. 11:27) and Shamhuth (27:8).

name: Sharar
summary: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:35); called also Sharar (2 Sam. 23:33).

name: Sharezer
summary: (god) protect the king!, a son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria. He and his brother Adrammelech murdered their father, and then fled into the land of Armenia (2 Kings 19:37).

name: Sheba (son of Raamah)
summary: Heb. shebha, the son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7), whose descendants settled with those of Dedan on the Persian Gulf.

name: Sheba (son of Joktan)
summary: Heb. id. A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:28), probably the founder of the Sabeans.

name: Sheba
summary: Heb. id. A son of Jokshan, who was a son of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:3).

name: Shechaniah
summary: A priest whose sons are mentioned in 1 Chr. 3:21, 22.

name: Shechaniah
summary: The father of Shemaiah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:29).

name: Shechem
summary: A descendant of Manasseh (Num. 26:31; Josh. 17:2).

name: Shelemiah
summary: Father of one of those who accused Jeremiah to Zedekiah (Jer. 37:3; 38:1).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A Levite (1 Chr. 9:16).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A Levite in the time of David, who with 200 of his brethren took part in the bringing up of the ark from Obed-edom to Hebron (1 Chr. 15:8).

name: Shimei
summary: One of David’s mighty men who refused to acknowledge Adonijah as David’s successor (1 Kings 1:8). He is probably the same person who is called elsewhere (4:18) “the son of Elah.”

name: Shimei
summary: A Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:26, 27).

name: Shimei
summary: A Levite (2 Chr. 31:12, 13).

name: Shimrith
summary: The mother of Jehozabad, who murdered Joash (2 Kings 12:21); called also Shimrith, a Moabitess (2 Chr. 24:26).

name: Shobai
summary: Captors (Ezra 2:42).

name: Shuah
summary: One of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2; Chr. 1:32).

name: Shubael
summary: One of the sons of Heman; one of those whose duty it was to “lift up the horn” in the temple service (1 Chr. 25:4, 5); called also Shubael (ver. 20).

name: Simon
summary: One of the brothers of our Lord (Matt. 13:55; Mark 6:3).

name: Simon
summary: A leper of Bethany, in whose house Mary anointed our Lord’s head with ointment “as he sat at meat” (Matt. 26:6-13; Mark 14:3-9).

name: Sinite
summary: An inhabitant of Sin, near Arka (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

name: Sippai
summary: Extension, the son of the giant whom Sibbechai slew (2 Sam. 21:18); called also Sippai (1 Chr. 20:4).

name: Sisera
summary: The ancestor of some of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55).

name: Sopater
summary: The father who saves, probably the same as Sosipater, a kinsman of Paul (Rom. 16:21), a Christian of the city of Berea who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4-6).

name: Sosthenes
summary: Safe in strength, the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, who was seized and beaten by the mob in the presence of Gallio, the Roman governor, when he refused to proceed against Paul at the instigation of the Jews (Acts 18:12-17). The motives of this assault against Sosthenes are not recorded, nor is it mentioned whether it was made by Greeks or Romans. Some identify him, but without sufficient grounds, with one whom Paul calls “Sosthenes our brother,” a convert to the faith (1 Cor. 1:1).

name: Tabbaoth
summary: Impressions; rings, “the children of,” returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:43).

name: Tahpenes
summary: The wife of Pharaoh, who gave her sister in marriage to Hadad the Edomite (1 Kings 11:19, 20).

name: Tanhumeth
summary: Consolation, a Netophathite; one of the captains who supported Gedaliah (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8).

name: Tarshish (son of Javan)
summary: One of the “sons” of Javan (Gen. 10:4; 1 Chr. 1:7).

name: Tartan
summary: One of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17).

name: Teresh
summary: Severe, a eunuch or chamberlain in the palace of Ahasuerus, who conspired with another to murder him. The plot was detected by Mordecai, and the conspirators were put to death (Esther 2:21; 6:2).

name: Tertullus
summary: A modification of “Tertius;” a Roman advocate, whom the Jews employed to state their case against Paul in the presence of Felix (Acts 24:1-9). The charges he adduced against the apostle were, “First, that he created disturbances among the Romans throughout the empire, an offence against the Roman government (crimen majestatis). Secondly, that he was a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes; disturbed the Jews in the exercise of their religion, guaranteed by the state; introduced new gods, a thing prohibited by the Romans. And thirdly, that he attempted to profane the temple, a crime which the Jews were permitted to punish.”

name: Theophilus
summary: Lover of God, a Christian, probably a Roman, to whom Luke dedicated both his Gospel (Luke 1:3) and the Acts of the Apostles (1:1). Nothing beyond this is known of him. From the fact that Luke applies to him the title “most excellent”, the same title Paul uses in addressing Felix (Acts 23:26; 24:3) and Festus (26:25), it has been concluded that Theophilus was a person of rank, perhaps a Roman officer.

name: Tibni
summary: Building of Jehovah, the son of Ginath, a man of some position, whom a considerable number of the people chose as monarch. For the period of four years he contended for the throne with Omri (1 Kings 16:21, 22), who at length gained the mastery, and became sole monarch of Israel.

name: Tidal
summary: (in the LXX. called “Thorgal”), styled the “king of nations” (Gen. 14:1-9). Mentioned as Tudkhula on Arioch’s brick (see facing page 139). Goyyim, translated “nations,” is the country called Gutium, east of Tigris and north of Elam.

name: Timnah
summary: A “duke” or sheik of Edom (Gen. 36:40).

name: Tiras
summary: The youngest of the sons of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5).

name: Tirhakah
summary: The last king of Egypt of the Ethiopian (the fifteenth) dynasty. He was the brother-in-law of So (q.v.). He probably ascended the throne about B.C. 692, having been previously king of Ethiopia (2 Kings 19:9; Isa. 37:9), which with Egypt now formed one nation. He was a great warrior, and but little is known of him. The Assyrian armies under Esarhaddon, and again under Assur-bani-pal, invaded Egypt and defeated Tirhakah, who afterwards retired into Ethiopia, where he died, after reigning twenty-six years.

name: Unni
summary: A Levite whom David appointed to take part in bringing the ark up to Jerusalem from the house of Obed-edom by playing the psaltery on that occasion (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

name: Uriel
summary: A Kohathite ancestor of the prophet Samuel (1 Chr. 6:36).

name: Uriel
summary: The chief of the Kohathites at the time when the ark was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:5, 11).

name: Uz (son of Aram)
summary: The son of Aram, and grandson of Shem (Gen. 10:23; 1 Chr. 1:17).

name: Uz (son of Dishan)
summary: One of the Horite “dukes” in the land of Edom (Gen. 36:28).

name: Uzal
summary: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

name: Uzzi
summary: A grandson of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:2, 3).

name: Uzziel
summary: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4); called also Azareel (18).

name: Zabad
summary: The son of Shemath. He conspired against Joash, king of Judah, and slew him (2 Chr. 24:25, 26). He is called also Jozachar (2 Kings 12:21).

name: Zaccai
summary: Pure, one whose “sons” returned with Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:9; Neh. 7:14).

name: Zacher
summary: Memorial, a son of Jehiel (1 Chr. 8:31; 9:35); called Zechariah (9:37).

name: Zadok
summary: The father of Jerusha, who was wife of King Uzziah, and mother of King Jotham (2 Kings 15:33; 2 Chr. 27:1).

name: Zavan
summary: Terror, one of the “dukes of Edom” (Gen. 36:27); called also Zavan (1 Chr. 1:42).

name: Zechariah
summary: The father of Abijah, who was the mother of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:1).

name: Zelek
summary: Cleft, an Ammonite; one of David’s valiant men (2 Sam. 23:37).

name: Zemarite
summary: The designation of one of the Phoenician tribes (Gen. 10:18) who inhabited the town of Sumra, at the western base of the Lebanon range. In the Amarna tablets (B.C. 1400) Zemar, or Zumur, was one of the most important of the Phoenician cities, but it afterwards almost disappears from history.

name: Zephaniah
summary: The father of Josiah, the priest who dwelt in Jerusalem when Darius issued the decree that the temple should be rebuilt (Zech. 6:10).

name: Zerah
summary: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:21, 41).

name: Zetham
summary: Olive planter, a Levite (1 Chr. 23:8).

name: Zibeon
summary: A Hivite (Gen. 36:2).

name: Zibiah
summary: The mother of King Joash (2 Kings 12:1; 2 Chr. 24:1).

name: Zichri
summary: A Levite, one of the sons of Asaph (Neh. 11:17); probably the same as Zichri (1 Chr. 9:15), and Zaccur (Neh. 12:35).

name: Zidon
summary: A fishery, a town on the Mediterranean coast, about 25 miles north of Tyre. It received its name from the “first-born” of Canaan, the grandson of Noah (Gen. 10:15, 19). It was the first home of the Phoenicians on the coast of Palestine, and from its extensive commercial relations became a “great” city (Josh. 11:8; 19:28). It was the mother city of Tyre. It lay within the lot of the tribe of Asher, but was never subdued (Judg. 1:31). The Zidonians long oppressed Israel (Judg. 10:12). From the time of David its glory began to wane, and Tyre, its “virgin daughter” (Isa. 23:12), rose to its place of pre-eminence. Solomon entered into a matrimonial alliance with the Zidonians, and thus their…

name: Ziha
summary: The name of a family of Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

name: Zimmah
summary: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:20).

name: Zimran
summary: Vine-dressers; celebrated, one of the sons of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

name: Ziph
summary: A son of Jehaleleel (1 Chr. 4:16).

name: Zizah
summary: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 23:11).

name: Zohar
summary: The father of Ephron the Hittite (Gen. 23:8).

name: Zophah
summary: Spreading out, a son of Helem (1 Chr. 7:35), a chief of Asher.

name: Zur
summary: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites defeated and put to death (Num. 31:8).

name: Zur
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:30).

name: Abagtha
summary: One of the seven eunuchs in Ahasuerus’s court (Esther 1:10; 2:21).

name: Abda
summary: The father of Adoniram, whom Solomon set over the tribute (1 Kings 4:6); i.e., the forced labour (R.V., “levy”).

name: Abdeel
summary: Servant of God, (Jer. 36:26), the father of Shelemiah.

name: Abdi
summary: Ezra 10:26.

name: Abdiel
summary: Servant of God, (1 Chr. 5:15), a Gadite chief.

name: Abdon
summary: One of the “sons” of Shashak (1 Chr. 8:23). This is the name also of a Levitical town of the Gershonites, in the tribe of Asher (Josh. 21:30; 1 Chr. 6:74). The ruins of Abdeh, some 8 miles north-east of Accho, probably mark its site.

name: Abiah
summary: One of the sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8). “Abiah,” A.V.

name: Abiel (Arbathite)
summary: An Arbathite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:32); called also Abi-albon (2 Sam. 23:31).

name: Abihail
summary: The second wife of King Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:18), a descendant of Eliab, David’s eldest brother.

name: Abihud
summary: One of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:3); called also Ahihud (ver. 7).

name: Abijah
summary: A son of Jeroboam, the first king of Israel. On account of his severe illness when a youth, his father sent his wife to consult the prophet Ahijah regarding his recovery. The prophet, though blind with old age, knew the wife of Jeroboam as soon as she approached, and under a divine impulse he announced to her that inasmuch as in Abijah alone of all the house of Jeroboam there was found “some good thing toward the Lord,” he only would come to his grave in peace. As his mother crossed the threshold of the door on her return, the youth died, and “all Israel mourned for him” (1 Kings 14:1-18).

name: Abinadab
summary: One of Solomon’s officers, who “provided victuals for the king and his household.” He presided, for this purpose, over the district of Dor (1 Kings 4:11).

name: Abiram
summary: The eldest son of Hiel the Bethelite, who perished prematurely in consequence of his father’s undertaking to rebuild Jericho (1 Kings 16:34), according to the words of Joshua (6:26).

name: Abishua
summary: The grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:4).

name: Abitub
summary: Father of goodness, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:11).

name: Abiud
summary: A descendant of Zerubbabel and father of Eliakim (Matt. 1:13, “Abiud”); called also Juda (Luke 3:26), and Obadiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

name: Achaicus
summary: (1 Cor. 16:17), one of the members of the church of Corinth who, with Fortunatus and Stephanas, visited Paul while he was at Ephesus, for the purpose of consulting him on the affairs of the church. These three probably were the bearers of the letter from Corinth to the apostle to which he alludes in 1 Cor. 7:1.

name: Addar
summary: Ample, splendid, son of Bela (1 Chr. 8:3); called also “Ard” (Gen. 46:21)

name: Addi
summary: Ornament, (Luke 3:28), the son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the progenitors of Christ.

name: Adiel
summary: A family head of the tribe of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

name: Adina
summary: Slender, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:42), a Reubenite.

name: Adino
summary: The Eznite, one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:8).

name: Adnah
summary: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Adnah
summary: A general under Jehoshaphat, chief over 300,000 men (2 Chr. 17:14).

name: Adonijah
summary: A Levite sent with the princes to teach the book of the law to the inhabitants of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Adonijah
summary: One of the “chiefs of the people” after the Captivity (Neh. 10:16).

name: Adrammelech
summary: An idol; a form of the sun-god worshipped by the inhabitants of Sepharvaim (2 Kings 17:31), and brought by the Sepharvite colonists into Samaria.

name: Agag
summary: A king of the Amalekites referred to by Balaam (Num. 24:7). He lived at the time of the Exodus.

name: Agee
summary: Fugitive, the father of Shammah, who was one of David’s mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11)

name: Agur
summary: Gatherer; the collector, mentioned as author of the sayings in Prov. 30. Nothing is known of him beyond what is there recorded.

name: Ahiah
summary: One of Solomon’s secretaries (1 Kings 4:3).

name: Ahiah
summary: One of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:7, R.V.). In A.V. called “Ahiah.”

name: Ahiezer
summary: The chief of the Benjamite slingers that repaired to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Ahihud
summary: Name different in Hebrew, meaning brother of Judah. Chief of the tribe of Asher; one of those appointed by Moses to superintend the division of Canaan among the tribe (Num. 34:27).

name: Ahihud
summary: A son of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:7).

name: Ahijah
summary: One of the five sons of Jerahmeel, who was great-grandson of Judah (1 Chr. 2:25).

name: Ahijah
summary: A Pelonite, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:36); called also Eliam (2 Sam. 23:34).

name: Ahijah
summary: A Levite having charge of the sacred treasury in the temple (1 Chr. 26:20).

name: Ahimaaz
summary: The father Ahinoam, the wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

name: Ahiman
summary: One of the guardians of the temple after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:17).

name: Ahinadab
summary: Brother of liberality = liberal, one of the twelve commissariat officers appointed by Solomon in so many districts of his kingdom to raise supplies by monthly rotation for his household. He was appointed to the district of Mahanaim (1 Kings 4:14), east of Jordan.

name: Ahinoam
summary: The daughter of Ahimaaz, and wife of Saul (1 Sam. 14:50).

name: Ahio
summary: One of the sons of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:14).

name: Ahishar
summary: Brother of song = singer, the officer who was “over the household” of Solomon (1 Kings 4:6).

name: Ahoah
summary: Brotherly, one of the sons of Bela, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:4). He is also called Ahiah (ver. 7) and Iri (1 Chr. 7:7). His descendants were called Ahohites (2 Sam. 23:9, 28).

name: Akkub
summary: A descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:24).

name: Akkub
summary: The head of one of the families of Nethinim (Ezra 2:45).

name: Alameth
summary: One of the nine sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

name: Alexander
summary: A man whose father, Simon the Cyrenian, bore the cross of Christ (Mark 15:21).

name: Alexander (Son of Simon)
summary: A relative of Annas the high priest, present when Peter and John were examined before the Sanhedrim (Acts 4:6).

name: Alexander (Jew of Ephesus)
summary: A Jew of Ephesus who took a prominent part in the uproar raised there by the preaching of Paul (Acts 19:33). The Jews put him forward to plead their cause before the mob. It was probably intended that he should show that he and the other Jews had no sympathy with Paul any more than the Ephesians had. It is possible that this man was the same as the following.

name: Alphaeus
summary: The father of Levi, or Matthew (Mark 2:14).

name: Amariah
summary: A “chief priest” who took an active part in the reformation under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 19:11); probably the same as mentioned in 1 Chr. 6:9.

name: Amariah
summary: One of the high priests in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 31:15).

name: Amariah
summary: Ezra 10:42.

name: Amariah
summary: Zeph. 1:1.

name: Amasa
summary: A son of Hadlai, and chief of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12) in the reign of Ahaz.

name: Amasai
summary: The leader of a body of men who joined David in the “stronghold,” probably of Adullam (1 Chr. 12:18).

name: Amasai
summary: One of the priests appointed to precede the ark with blowing of trumpets on its removal from the house of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Amasai
summary: The father of a Levite, one of the two Kohathites who took a prominent part at the instance of Hezekiah in the cleansing of the temple (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Amasiah
summary: Burden of (i.e., “sustained by”) Jehovah, the “son of Zichri, who willingly offered himself unto the Lord,” a captain over thousands under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:16; comp. Judg. 5:9).

name: Amaziah
summary: The father of Joshah, one of the Simeonite chiefs in the time of Hezekiah (1 Chr. 4:34).

name: Amaziah
summary: A Levite, son of Hilkiah, of the descendants of Ethan the Merarite (1 Chr. 6:45).

name: Ammiel
summary: One of the twelve spies sent by Moses to search the land of Canaan (Num. 13:12). He was one of the ten who perished by the plague for their unfavourable report (Num. 14:37).

name: Ammiel
summary: One of the sons of Obed-edom the Levite (1 Chr. 26:5).

name: Ammihud
summary: The father of Talmai, king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after the murder of Amnon (2 Sam. 13:37).

name: Ammihud
summary: The son of Omri, and the father of Uthai (1 Chr. 9:4).

name: Ammizabad
summary: People of the giver, the son of Benaiah, who was the third and chief captain of the host under David (1 Chr. 27:6).

name: Amnon
summary: One of the sons of Shammai, of the children of Ezra (1 Chr. 4:20; comp. 17).

name: Amplias
summary: A Roman Christian saluted by Paul (Rom. 16:8).

name: Amram
summary: Ezra 10:34.

name: Anammelech
summary: One of the gods worshipped by the people of Sepharvaim, who colonized Samaria (2 Kings 17:31). The name means “Anu is king.” It was a female deity representing the moon, as Adrammelech (q.v.) was the male representing the sun.

name: Anan
summary: Cloud, one of the Israelites who sealed the covenant after the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:26).

name: Andronicus
summary: Man-conquering, a Jewish Christian, the kinsman and fellowprisoner of Paul (Rom. 16:7); “of note among the apostles.”

name: Anna
summary: Grace, an aged widow, the daughter of Phanuel. She was a “prophetess,” like Miriam, Deborah, and Huldah (2 Chr. 34:22). After seven years of married life her husband died, and during her long widowhood she daily attended the temple services. When she was eighty-four years old, she entered the temple at the moment when the aged Simeon uttered his memorable words of praise and thanks to God that he had fulfilled his ancient promise in sending his Son into the world (Luke 2:36, 37).

name: Antipas
summary: A “faithful martyr” (Rev. 2:13), of whom nothing more is certainly known.

name: Apelles
summary: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:10), and styles “approved in Christ.”

name: Apollyon
summary: Destruction, the Hebrew name (equivalent to the Greek Apollyon, i.e., destroyer) of “the angel of the bottomless pit” (Rev. 9:11). It is rendered “destruction” in Job 28:22; 31:12; 26:6; Prov. 15:11; 27:20. In the last three of these passages the Revised Version retains the word “Abaddon.” We may regard this word as a personification of the idea of destruction, or as sheol, the realm of the dead.

name: Apphia
summary: Increasing, a female Christian at Colosse (Philemon 1:2), supposed by some to have been the wife of Philemon.

name: Aram (son of Kemuel)
summary: The son of Shem (Gen. 10:22); according to Gen. 22:21, a grandson of Nahor. In Matt. 1:3, 4, and Luke 3:33, this word is the Greek form of Ram, the father of Amminadab (1 Chr. 2:10). The word means high, or highlands, and as the name of a country denotes that elevated region extending from the northeast of Palestine to the Euphrates. It corresponded generally with the Syria and Mesopotamia of the Greeks and Romans. In Gen. 25:20; 31:20, 24; Deut. 26:5, the word “Syrian” is properly “Aramean” (R.V., marg.). Damascus became at length the capital of the several smaller kingdoms comprehended under the designation “Aram” or “Syria.”

name: Archelaus
summary: Ruler of the people, son of Herod the Great, by Malthace, a Samaritan woman. He was educated along with his brother Antipas at Rome. He inherited from his father a third part of his kingdom viz., Idumea, Judea, and Samaria, and hence is called “king” (Matt. 2:22). It was for fear of him that Joseph and Mary turned aside on their way back from Egypt. Till a few days before his death Herod had named Antipas as his successor, but in his last moments he named Archelaus.

name: Ard
summary: Descent, a grandson of Benjamin (Num. 26:38-40). In 1 Chr. 8:3 he is called Addar. His descendants are mentioned in Num. 26:40.

name: Ardon
summary: Descendant, the last of the three sons of Caleb by his first wife Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

name: Aretas
summary: The father-in-law of Herod Antipas, and king of Arabia Petraea. His daughter returned to him on the occasion of her husband’s entering into an adulterous alliance with Herodias, the wife of Herod-Philip, his half-brother (Luke 3:19, 20; Mark 6:17; Matt. 14:3). This led to a war between Aretas and Herod Antipas. Herod’s army was wholly destroyed (A.D. 36). Aretas, taking advantage of the complications of the times on account of the death of the Emperor Tiberius (A.D. 37), took possession of Damascus (2 Cor. 11:32; comp. Acts 9:25). At this time Paul returned to Damascus from Arabia.

name: Arieh
summary: The lion, the name of one of the body-guard slain with Pekahiah at Samaria (2 Kings 15:25) by the conspirator Pekah.

name: Ariel
summary: One of the chief men sent by Ezra to procure Levites for the sanctuary (Ezra 8:16).

name: Armoni
