summary: Inhabitant of a fortress, the first-named of the two sons of Saul and Rizpah. He was delivered up to the Gibeonites by David, and hanged by them (2 Sam. 21:8, 9).

name: Asaph
summary: The “keeper of the king’s forest,” to whom Nehemiah requested from Artaxerxes a “letter” that he might give him timber for the temple at Jerusalem (Neh. 2:8).

name: Ashpenaz
summary: The master of the eunuchs of Nebuchadnezzar (Dan. 1:3), the “Rabsaris” of the court. His position was similar to that of the Kislar-aga of the modern Turkish sultans.

name: Asnappar
summary: Probably the same as Assur-bani-pal (Sardanapalos of the Greeks), styled the “great and noble” (Ezra 4:10), was the son and successor (B.C. 668) of Esar-haddon (q.v.). He was “luxurious, ambitious, and cruel, but a magnificent patron of literature.” He formed at Nineveh a library of clay tablets, numbering about 10,000. These are now mostly in the British Museum. They throw much light on the history and antiquities of Assyria. Assur-bani-pal was a munificent patron of literature, and the conqueror of Elam. Towards the middle of his reign his empire was shaken by a great rebellion headed by his brother in Babylon. The rebellion was finally put down, but Egypt was lost, and the military power…

name: Athaliah
summary: Ezra 8:7.

name: Azariah
summary: Son of Ethan, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:8).

name: Azariah
summary: The son of Oded, a remarkable prophet in the days of Asa (2 Chr. 15:1). He stirred up the king and the people to a great national reformation.

name: Azaziah
summary: One of the Levitical harpers in the temple (1 Chr. 15:21).

name: Azaziah
summary: The father of Hoshea, who was made ruler over the Ephraimites (1 Chr. 27:20).

name: Azaziah
summary: One who had charge of the temple offerings (2 Chr. 31:13).

name: Azmaveth
summary: An overseer over the royal treasury in the time of David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:25).

name: Azur
summary: The father of Hananiah, a false prophet (Jer. 28:1).

name: Azur
summary: The father of Jaazaniah (Ezek. 11:1).

name: Azzur
summary: One of those who sealed the covenant with Jehovah on the return from Babylon (Neh. 10:17).

name: Baalhanan
summary: An overseer of “the olive trees and sycomore trees in the low plains” (the Shephelah) under David (1 Chr. 27:28).

name: Baalis
summary: King of the Ammonites at the time of the Babylonian captivity (Jer. 40:14). He hired Ishmael to slay Gedaliah who had been appointed governor over the cities of Judah.

name: Baana
summary: One of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:12).

name: Baana
summary: Father of Zadok (Neh. 3:4).

name: Baanah
summary: Son of Hushai, another of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:16).

name: Bani
summary: One of David’s thirty-seven warriors, a Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

name: Bariah
summary: Fugitive, one of Shemaiah’s five sons. Their father is counted along with them in 1 Chr. 3:22.

name: Barsabas Justus
summary: Surnamed Barsabas (Acts 1:23); also called Justus. He was one of those who “companied with the apostles all the time that the Lord Jesus went out and in among them” (Acts 1:21), and was one of the candidates for the place of Judas.

name: Bartimaeus
summary: Son of Timaeus, one of the two blind beggars of Jericho (Mark 10:46; Matt. 20:30). His blindness was miraculously cured on the ground of his faith.

name: Barzillai
summary: A Meholathite, the father of Adriel (2 Sam. 21:8).

name: Bealiah
summary: Whose Lord is Jehovah, a Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes of the sling and bow (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Bedan
summary: One of the judges of Israel (1 Sam. 12:11). It is uncertain who he was. Some suppose that Barak is meant, others Samson, but most probably this is a contracted form of Abdon (Judg. 12:13).

name: Beeri
summary: The father of Judith, one of the wives of Esau (Gen. 26:34), the same as Adah (Gen. 36:2).

name: Bela
summary: A son of Azaz (1 Chr. 5:8).

name: Benaiah
summary: The son of Jeiel (2 Chr. 20:14).

name: Bera
summary: Gift, or son of evil, king of Sodom at the time of the invasion of the four kings under Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2, 8, 17, 21).

name: Berachah
summary: One of the Benjamite warriors, Saul’s brethren, who joined David when at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Berechiah
summary: The fourth of the five sons of Zerubbabel, of the royal family of Judah (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Berechiah
summary: One of the seven Ephraimite chieftains, son of Meshillemoth (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Bered
summary: A son of Shuthelah, and grandson of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20).

name: Beriah
summary: A son of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20-23), born after the slaughter of his brothers, and so called by his father “because it went evil with his house” at that time.

name: Bezer
summary: A descendant of Asher (1 Chr. 7:37).

name: Bigtha
summary: Garden, or gift of fortune, one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains who had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10).

name: Bilgah
summary: The head of the fifteenth sacerdotal course for the temple service (1 Chr. 24:14).

name: Birsha
summary: Son of wickedness, a king of Gomorrah whom Abraham succoured in the invasion of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

name: Blastus
summary: Chamberlain to king Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:20). Such persons generally had great influence with their masters.

name: Buz
summary: The second son of Nahor and Milcah, and brother of Huz (Gen. 22:21). Elihu was one of his descendants (Job 32:2).

name: Buz
summary: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Gad (1 Chr. 5:14).

name: Cainan (son of Arphaxad)
summary: The son of Arphaxad (Luke 3:36). He is nowhere named in the Old Testament. He is usually called the “second Cainan.”

name: Calcol
summary: (1 Chr. 2:6), sustenance, the same probably as Chalcol (1 Kings 4:31), one of the four sages whom Solomon excelled in wisdom; for “he was wiser than all men.”

name: Candace
summary: The queen of the Ethiopians whose “eunuch” or chamberlain was converted to Christianity by the instrumentality of Philip the evangelist (Acts 8:27). The country which she ruled was called by the Greeks Meroe, in Upper Nubia. It was long the centre of commercial intercourse between Africa and the south of Asia, and hence became famous for its wealth (Isa. 45:14). It is somewhat singular that female sovereignty seems to have prevailed in Ethiopia, the name Candace (compare “Pharaoh,” “Ptolemy,” “Caesar”) being a title common to several successive queens. It is probable that Judaism had taken root in Ethiopia at this time, and hence the visit of the queen’s treasurer to Jerusalem to keep the…

name: Chenaanah
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 7:10).

name: Chesed
summary: Gain, the son of Nahor (Gen. 22:22).

name: Chloe
summary: Verdure, a female Christian (1 Cor. 1:11), some of whose household had informed Paul of the divided state of the Corinthian church. Nothing is known of her.

name: Claudia
summary: A female Christian mentioned in 2 Tim. 4:21. It is a conjecture having some probability that she was a British maiden, the daughter of king Cogidunus, who was an ally of Rome, and assumed the name of the emperor, his patron, Tiberius Claudius, and that she was the wife of Pudens.

name: Claudius Lysias
summary: Claudius Lysias, a Greek who, having obtained by purchase the privilege of Roman citizenship, took the name of Claudius (Acts 21:31-40; 22:28; 23:26).

name: Clement
summary: Mild, a Christian of Philippi, Paul’s “fellow-labourer,” whose name he mentions as “in the book of life” (Phil. 4:3). It was an opinion of ancient writers that he was the Clement of Rome whose name is well known in church history, and that he was the author of an Epistle to the Corinthians, the only known manuscript of which is appended to the Alexandrian Codex, now in the British Museum. It is of some historical interest, and has given rise to much discussion among critics. It makes distinct reference to Paul’s First Epistle to the Corinthians.

name: Conaniah
summary: Whom Jehovah hath set, a Levite placed over the tithes brought into the temple (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Coz
summary: A descendant of Judah. 1 Chr. 4:8, “Coz;” R.V., “Hakkoz.”

name: Crescens
summary: Increasing, probably one of the seventy disciples of Christ. He was one of Paul’s assistants (2 Tim. 4:10), probably a Christian of Rome.

name: Cyrenius
summary: The Grecized form of Quirinus. His full name was Publius Sulpicius Quirinus. Recent historical investigation has proved that Quirinus was governor of Cilicia, which was annexed to Syria at the time of our Lord’s birth. Cilicia, which he ruled, being a province of Syria, he is called the governor, which he was de jure, of Syria. Some ten years afterwards he was appointed governor of Syria for the second time. During his tenure of office, at the time of our Lord’s birth (Luke 2:2), a “taxing” (R.V., “enrolment;” i.e., a registration) of the people was “first made;” i.e., was made for the first time under his government.

name: Damaris
summary: A heifer, an Athenian woman converted to Christianity under the preaching of Paul (Acts 17:34). Some have supposed that she may have been the wife of Dionysius the Areopagite.

name: Darda
summary: Pearl of wisdom, one of the four who were noted for their wisdom, but whom Solomon excelled (1 Kings 4:31).

name: Darius
summary: Darius the Persian (Neh. 12:22) was probably the Darius II. (Ochus or Nothus) of profane history, the son of Artaxerxes Longimanus, who was the son and successor of Ahasuerus (Xerxes). There are some, however, who think that the king here meant was Darius III. (Codomannus), the antagonist of Alexander the Great (B.C. 336-331).

name: Debir
summary: The king of Eglon, one of the five Canaanitish kings who were hanged by Joshua (Josh. 10:3, 23) after the victory at Gibeon. These kings fled and took refuge in a cave at Makkedah. Here they were kept confined till Joshua returned from the pursuit of their discomfited armies, when he caused them to be brought forth, and “Joshua smote them, and slew them, and hanged them on five trees” (26).

name: Delaiah
summary: The head of the twenty-third division of the priestly order (1 Chr. 24:18).

name: Diblaim
summary: Doubled cakes, the mother of Gomer, who was Hosea’s wife (Hos. 1:3).

name: Dionysius
summary: The Areopagite, one of Paul’s converts at Athens (Acts 17:34).

name: Dodo
summary: A descendant of Issachar (Judg. 10:1).

name: Drusilla
summary: Third and youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:1-4, 20-23). Felix, the Roman procurator of Judea, induced her to leave her husband, Azizus, the king of Emesa, and become his wife. She was present with Felix when Paul reasoned of “righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come” (Acts 24:24). She and her son perished in the eruption of Mount Vesuvius, A.D. 79.

name: Eber (a Benjamite)
summary: The oldest of the three sons of Elpaal the Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:12).

name: Eber (Amok Family Head)
summary: The head of the priestly family of Amok in the time of Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:20).

name: Eden
summary: Son of Joah, and one of the Levites who assisted in reforming the public worship of the sanctuary in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Ehud
summary: A descendant of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10), his great-grandson.

name: Elah
summary: The second of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

name: Elasah
summary: The son of Shaphan, one of the two who were sent by Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and also took charge of Jeremiah’s letter to the captives in Babylon (Jer. 29:3).

name: Eleazar
summary: An inhabitant of Kirjath-jearim who was “sanctified” to take charge of the ark, although not allowed to touch it, while it remained in the house of his father Abinadab (1 Sam. 7:1, 2; comp. Num. 3:31; 4:15).

name: Eleazar
summary: A son of Phinehas associated with the priests in taking charge of the sacred vessels brought back to Jerusalem after the Exile (Ezra 8:33).

name: Eliab
summary: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in his stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:9).

name: Eliada
summary: A mighty man of war, a Benjamite (2 Chr. 17:17).

name: Eliadah
summary: An Aramite of Zobah, captain of a marauding band that troubled Solomon (1 Kings 11:23).

name: Eliakim
summary: The son of Abiud, of the posterity of Zerubbabel (Matt. 1:13).

name: Eliakim
summary: The son of Melea (Luke 3:30), and probably grandson of Nathan.

name: Eliam
summary: This name also occurs as that of a Gilonite, the son of Ahithophel, and one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:34). perhaps these two were the same person.

name: Eliashib
summary: A priest, head of one of the courses of the priests of the time of David (1 Chr. 24:12).

name: Elidad
summary: Whom God has loved, son of Chislon, and chief of the tribe of Benjamin; one of those who were appointed to divide the Promised Land among the tribes (Num. 34:21).

name: Eliel
summary: A chief of Manasseh, on the east of Jordan (1 Chr. 5:24).

name: Eliel
summary: A Gadite who joined David in the hold at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:11).

name: Eliel
summary: One of the overseers of the offerings in the reign of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 31:13).

name: Eliezer (Abraham's Steward)
summary: “Of Damascus,” the “steward” (R.V., “possessor”) of Abraham’s house (Gen. 15:2, 3). It was probably he who headed the embassy sent by Abraham to the old home of his family in Padan-aram to seek a wife for his son Isaac. The account of this embassy is given at length in Gen. 24.

name: Eliezer
summary: The son of Becher, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

name: Eliezer
summary: One of the priests who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Eliezer
summary: Son of Zichri, and chief of the Reubenites under David (1 Chr. 27:16).

name: Eliezer
summary: A prophet in the time of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 20:37). Others of this name are mentioned Luke 3:29; Ezra 8:16; 10:18, 23, 31.

name: Elihu
summary: One of the captains of thousands of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Elihu
summary: One of the family of Obed-edom, who were appointed porters of the temple under David (1 Chr. 26:7).

name: Elika
summary: God is his rejector, one of David’s thirty-seven distinguished heros (2 Sam. 23:25).

name: Eliphelet
summary: One of David’s distinguished warriors (2 Sam. 23:34); called also Eliphal in 1 Chr. 11:35.

name: Eliphelet
summary: A descendant of king Saul through Jonathan (1 Chr. 8:39).

name: Elishama
summary: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the people the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Elishaphat
summary: Whom God has judged, one of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in the league to overthrow the usurpation of Athaliah (2 Chr. 23:1).

name: Elisheba
summary: God is her oath, the daughter of Amminadab and the wife of Aaron (Ex. 6:23).

name: Epaenetus
summary: Commendable, a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutation (Rom. 16:5). He is spoken of as “the first fruits of Achaia” (R.V., “of Asia”, i.e., of proconsular Asia, which is probably the correct reading). As being the first convert in that region, he was peculiarly dear to the apostle. He calls him his “well beloved.”

name: Ephah
summary: 1 Chr. 2:46, a concubine of Caleb.

name: Ephah
summary: 1 Chr. 2:47, a descendant of Judah. Ephah, a word of Egyptian origin, meaning measure; a grain measure containing “three seahs or ten omers,” and equivalent to the bath for liquids (Ex. 16:36; 1 Sam. 17:17; Zech. 5:6). The double ephah in Prov. 20:10 (marg., “an ephah and an ephah”), Deut. 25:14, means two ephahs, the one false and the other just.

name: Epher
summary: The head of one of the families of trans-Jordanic Manasseh who were carried captive by Tiglath-pileser (1 Chr. 5:24).

name: Ethan
summary: “The Ezrahite,” distinguished for his wisdom (1 Kings 4:31). He is named as the author of the 89th Psalm. He was of the tribe of Levi.

name: Ethbaal
summary: With Baal, a king of Sidon (B.C. 940-908), father of Jezebel, who was the wife of Ahab (1 Kings 16:31). He is said to have been also a priest of Astarte, whose worship was closely allied to that of Baal, and this may account for his daughter’s zeal in promoting idolatry in Israel. This marriage of Ahab was most fatal to both Israel and Judah. Dido, the founder of Carthage, was his granddaughter.

name: Euodias
summary: A good journey, a female member of the church at Philippi. She was one who laboured much with Paul in the gospel. He exhorts her to be of one mind with Syntyche (Phil. 4:2). From this it seems they had been at variance with each other.

name: Eutychus
summary: Fortunate, (Acts 20:9-12), a young man of Troas who fell through drowsiness from the open window of the third floor of the house where Paul was preaching, and was “taken up dead.” The lattice-work of the window being open to admit the air, the lad fell out and down to the court below. Paul restored him to life again. (Comp. 1 Kings 17:21; 2 Kings 4:34.)

name: Ezer
summary: A Levite (Neh. 3:19).

name: Ezri
summary: Help of Jehovah, the son of Chelub. He superintended, under David, those who “did the work of the field for tillage” (1 Chr. 27:26).

name: Fortunatus
summary: Fortunate, a disciple of Corinth who visited Paul at Ephesus, and returned with Stephanas and Achaicus, the bearers of the apostle’s first letter to the Corinthians (1 Cor. 16:17).

name: Gaddi
summary: Fortunate, the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve “spies” sent by Moses to spy the land (Num. 13:11).

name: Gaddiel
summary: Fortune (i.e., sent) of God, the representative of the tribe of Zebulum among the twelve spies (Num. 13:10).

name: Gaius (of Macedonia)
summary: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14). During a heathen outbreak against Paul at Ephesus the mob seized Gaius and Aristarchus because they could not find Paul, and rushed with them into the theatre. Some have identified this Gaius with No. (2).

name: Gaius (of Derbe)
summary: A man of Derbe who accompanied Paul into Asia on his last journey to Jerusalem

name: Gaius
summary: A Christain of Asia Minor to whom John addressed his third epistle (3 John 1:1).

name: Gamul
summary: Weaned the leader of one of the priestly courses (1 Chr. 24:17).

name: Geber
summary: A valiant man, (1 Kings 4:19), one of Solomon’s purveyors, having jurisdiction over a part of Gilead, comprising all the kingdom of Sihon and part of the kingdom of Og (Deut. 2; 31).

name: Gedaliah
summary: One of the Jewish nobles who conspired against Jeremiah (Jer. 38:1).

name: Gemariah
summary: The son of Hilkiah, who accompanied Shaphan with the tribute-money from Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and was the bearer at the same time of a letter from Jeremiah to the Jewish captives at Babylon (Jer. 29:3, 4).

name: Genubath
summary: Theft, the son of Hadad, of the Edomitish royal family. He was brought up in Pharaoh’s household. His mother was a sister of Tahpenes, the king of Egypt’s wife, mentioned in 1 Kings 11:20.

name: Gershom
summary: The son of Manasseh (Judg. 18:30), in R.V. “of Moses.”

name: Gershom
summary: A descendant of Phinehas who returned with Ezra from Babylon (Ezra 8:2).

name: Gog
summary: A Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:4), the father of Shimei.

name: Hadlai
summary: Resting, an Ephraimite; the father of Amasa, mentioned in 2 Chr. 28:12.

name: Hakkoz
summary: The thorn, the head of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:10).

name: Hammoleketh
summary: The queen, the daughter of Machir and sister of Gilead (1 Chr. 7:17, 18). Abiezer was one of her three children.

name: Hanan
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:23).

name: Hanan
summary: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:43).

name: Hanan
summary: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:22).

name: Hananiah
summary: A chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:24).

name: Hananiah
summary: One of Uzziah’s military officers (2 Chr. 26:11).

name: Hananiah
summary: Ezra 10:28.

name: Hananiah
summary: The “ruler of the palace; he was a faithful man, and feared God above many” (Neh. 7:2).

name: Hananiah
summary: A priest, son of Jeremiah (Neh. 12:12).

name: Hananiah
summary: Grandfather of the captain who arrested Jeremiah (Jer. 37:13).

name: Haniel
summary: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:39).

name: Hanniel
summary: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 34:23).

name: Haran (son of Caleb)
summary: The son of Caleb of Judah (1 Chr. 2:46) by his concubine Ephah.

name: Harbona
summary: (a Persian word meaning “ass-driver”), one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains of king Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10; 7:9).

name: Harhaiah
summary: Zeal of Jehovah, (Neh. 3:8) “of the goldsmiths,” one whose son helped to repair the wall of Jerusalem.

name: Harnepher
summary: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:36).

name: Harum
summary: Elevated, (1 Chr. 4:8), a descendant of Judah.

name: Haruz
summary: Eager, the father of Meshullemeth, the wife of king Manasseh (2 Kings 21:19) and mother of king Amon.

name: Hasadiah
summary: Favoured by Jehovah, one of the sons of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:20), of the royal line of David.

name: Hasenuah
summary: Bristling or hated, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 9:7).

name: Hashabiah
summary: One of the chief Levites (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Hashabiah
summary: A Levite (Neh. 11:22).

name: Hashabniah
summary: One of the Levites whom Ezra appointed to interpret the law to the people (Neh. 9:5).

name: Hashbadana
summary: Consideration in judging, stood at Ezra’s left hand when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Hashubah
summary: Ibid., a descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Hashum
summary: Stood on Ezra’s left hand while he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Hathath
summary: Terror, son of Othniel (1 Chr. 4:13).

name: Hattush
summary: Ezra 8:2.

name: Hazo
summary: Vision, one of the sons of Nahor (Gen. 22:22).

name: Heber
summary: One of the seven heads of the families of the Gadites (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Heber
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:17).

name: Helez
summary: One of Judah’s posterity (1 Chr. 2:39).

name: Heli
summary: Elevation, father of Joseph in the line of our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:23).

name: Helkai
summary: Smooth-tongued, one of the chief priests in the time of Joiakim (Neh. 12:15).

name: Heman
summary: 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chr. 2:6, a son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

name: Heman
summary: 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chr. 2:6, a son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

name: Hepher
summary: The second son of Asher (1 Chr. 4:6).

name: Hepher
summary: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:36).

name: Hermes
summary: Mercury, a Roman Christian (Rom. 16:14).

name: Hermogenes
summary: Mercury-born, at one time Paul’s fellow-labourer in Asia Minor, who, however, afterwards abandoned him, along with one Phygellus, probably on account of the perils by which they were beset (2 Tim. 1:15).

name: Herodion
summary: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes and calls his “kinsman” (Rom. 16:11).

name: Hezion
summary: Vision, the father of Tabrimon, and grandfather of Ben-hadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

name: Hezir
summary: The head of the seventeenth course of the priests (1 Chr. 24:15).

name: Hezir
summary: Neh. 10:20, one who sealed Nehemiah’s covenant.

name: Hiel
summary: Life of (i.e., from) God, a native of Bethel, who built (i.e., fortified) Jericho some seven hundred years after its destruction by the Israelites. There fell on him for such an act the imprecation of Joshua (6:26). He laid the foundation in his first-born, and set up the gates in his youngest son (1 Kings 16:34), i.e., during the progress of the work all his children died.

name: Hizkijah
summary: (Neh. 10:17), one who sealed the covenant.

name: Hodijah
summary: Neh. 10:18, a Levite who sealed the covenant.

name: Hoham
summary: Jehovah impels, the king of Hebron who joined the league against Gibeon. He and his allies were defeated (Josh. 10:3, 5, 16-27).

name: Hoshea
summary: 1 Chr. 27:20. The ruler of Ephraim in David’s time.

name: Iddo
summary: Timely. The father of Ahinadab, who was one of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:14).

name: Iddo
summary: Lovely. The son of Zechariah (1 Chr. 27:21), the ruler of Manasseh in David’s time.

name: Igal
summary: Num. 13:7, one of the spies of the tribe of Issachar.

name: Igal
summary: Son of Nathan of Zobah, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:36).

name: Immer
summary: The father of Zadok (Neh. 3:29).

name: Iphedeiah
summary: Set free by Jehovah, a chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:25).

name: Ira
summary: A Jairite and priest, a royal chaplain (2 Sam. 20:26) or confidential adviser (comp. 2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Chr. 18:17).

name: Irad
summary: Runner; wild ass, one of the antediluvian patriarchs, the father of Mehujael (Gen. 4:18), and grandson of Cain.

name: Iscah
summary: Spy, the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot (Gen. 11:29, 31).

name: Ishbi-benob
summary: My seat at Nob, one of the Rephaim, whose spear was three hundred shekels in weight. He was slain by Abishai (2 Sam. 21:16, 17).

name: Ishmaiah
summary: Son of Obadiah, and viceroy of Zebulun under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:19).

name: Ismaiah
summary: A Gibeonite who joined David at Ziklag, “a hero among the thirty and over the thirty” (1 Chr. 12:4).

name: Jaakobah
summary: Heel-catcher, a form of the name Jacob, one of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

name: Jaanai
summary: Mourner, one of the chief Gadites (1 Chr. 5:12).

name: Jaasiel
summary: Made by God, one of David’s body-guard, the son of Abner (1 Chr. 27:21), called Jasiel in 1 Chr. 11:47.

name: Jaazaniah
summary: The son of Jeremiah, and one of the chief Rechabites (Jer. 35:3).

name: Jaazaniah
summary: The son of Shaphan (Ezek. 8:11).

name: Jabal
summary: A stream, a descendant of Cain, and brother of Jubal; “the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle” (Gen. 4:20). This description indicates that he led a wandering life.

name: Jabin
summary: A king of Hazor, at the time of the entrance of Israel into Canaan (Josh. 11:1-14), whose overthrow and that of the northern chief with whom he had entered into a confederacy against Joshua was the crowning act in the conquest of the land (11:21-23; comp. 14:6-15). This great battle, fought at Lake Merom, was the last of Joshua’s battles of which we have any record. Here for the first time the Israelites encountered the iron chariots and horses of the Canaanites.

name: Jachan
summary: Mourner, one of the chief Gadite “brothers” in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Jachin
summary: The head of one of the courses (the twenty-first) of priests (1 Chr. 24:17).

name: Jaddua
summary: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:21).

name: Jadon
summary: Judge, a Meronothite who assisted in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:7).

name: Jahath
summary: One of the sons of Shelomoth, of the family of Kohath (1 Chr. 24:22).

name: Jahath
summary: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the overseers of the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

name: Jahaziel
summary: A priest who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:6).

name: Jahaziel
summary: The son of Zechariah, a Levite of the family of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14-17). He encouraged Jehoshaphat against the Moabites and Ammonites.

name: Jahdai
summary: Grasper, a descendant of Caleb, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:47).

name: Jahzerah
summary: Returner, the son of Meshullam, and father of Adiel (1 Chr. 9:12).

name: Jair
summary: A Benjamite, the father of Mordecai, Esther’s uncle (Esther 2:5).

name: Jakeh
summary: Pious, the father of Agur (Prov. 30:1). Nothing is known of him.

name: Jakim
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:19).

name: Jakim
summary: Chief of the twelfth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:12).

name: Jalon
summary: Lodger, the last of the four sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

name: Jambres
summary: One of those who opposed Moses in Egypt (2 Tim. 3:8).

name: Jannes
summary: One of the Egyptians who “withstood Moses” (2 Tim. 3:8).

name: Japhia
summary: The king of Lachish, who joined in the confederacy against Joshua (Josh. 10:3), and was defeated and slain. In one of the Amarna tablets he speaks of himself as king of Gezer. Called also Horam (Josh. 10:33).

name: Jarib
summary: One of the chiefs sent by Ezra to bring up the priests to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:16).

name: Jarib
summary: Ezra 10:18.

name: Jashen
summary: Sleeping, called also Hashem (1 Chr. 11:34); a person, several of whose sons were in David’s body-guard (2 Sam. 23:32).

name: Jashub
summary: Ezra 10:29.

name: Jedaiah
summary: Invoker of Jehovah. The son of Shimri, a chief Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Jedaiah
summary: One of those who repaired the walls of Jerusalem after the return from Babylon (Neh. 3:10).

name: Jediael
summary: A Shimrite, one of David’s bodyguard (1 Chr. 11:45). Probably same as in 12:20.

name: Jediael
summary: A Korhite of the family of Ebiasaph, and one of the gate-keepers to the temple (1 Chr. 26:2).

name: Jehaleleel
summary: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 4:16).

name: Jehalelel
summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Jehdeiah
summary: One of the Levitical attendants at the temple, a descendant of Shubael (1 Chr. 24:20).

name: Jehdeiah
summary: A Meronothite, herdsman of the asses under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:30).

name: Jehiel
summary: One of David’s guard (1 Chr. 11:44).

name: Jehiel
summary: A Hachmonite, a tutor in the family of David toward the close of his reign (1 Chr. 27:32).

name: Jehiel
summary: The second of Jehoshaphat’s six sons (2 Chr. 21:2).

name: Jehiel
summary: One of the Levites of the family of Heman who assisted Hezekiah in his work of reformation (2 Chr. 29:14).

name: Jehiel
summary: A “prince” and “ruler of the house of God” who contributed liberally to the renewal of the temple sacrifices under Josiah (2 Chr. 35:8).

name: Jehiel
summary: The father of Obadiah (Ezra 8:9).

name: Jehizkiah
summary: Jehovah strengthens, one of the chiefs of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Jehohanan
summary: A Korhite, the head of one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:3).

name: Jehohanan
summary: One of Jehoshaphat’s “captains” (2 Chr. 17:15).

name: Jehoiarib
summary: Jehovah defends, a priest at Jerusalem, head of one of the sacerdotal courses (1 Chr. 9:10; 24:7). His “course” went up from Babylon after the Exile (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42).

name: Jehonathan
summary: One of the stewards of David’s store-houses (1 Chr. 27:25).

name: Jehonathan
summary: A Levite who taught the law to the people of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Jehoram
summary: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to instructruct the people in Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Jehoshaphat
summary: Solomon’s purveyor in Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

name: Jehoshaphat
summary: One of the priests who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Jehozabad
summary: The son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), one of the Levite porters.

name: Jehu
summary: The son of Obed, and father of Azariah (1 Chr. 2:38).

name: Jehu
summary: One of the Benjamite slingers that joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Jeiel
summary: 1 Chr. 5:7. A Reubenite chief.

name: Jeiel
summary: 2 Chr. 26:11. A scribe.

name: Jeiel
summary: 2 Chr. 29:13. A Levite of the sons of Asaph.

name: Jeiel
summary: One of the chief Levites, who made an offering for the restoration of the Passover by Josiah (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Jeiel
summary: Ezra 8:13.

name: Jeiel
summary: Ezra 10:43.

name: Jemima
summary: Dove, the eldest of Job’s three daughters born after his time of trial (Job 42:14).

name: Jephunneh
summary: One of the descendants of Asher (1 Chr. 7:38).

name: Jerahmeel
summary: The son of Kish, a Levite (1 Chr. 24:29).

name: Jerahmeel
summary: Son of Hammelech (Jer. 36:26).

name: Jered
summary: A son of Ezra probably (1 Chr. 4:18).

name: Jeremiah
summary: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Manasseh on the east of Jordan (1 Chr. 5:24).

name: Jeremiah
summary: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

name: Jeremiah
summary: A Gadite who joined David in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:10).

name: Jeremiah
summary: A Gadite warrior (1 Chr. 12:13).

name: Jerimoth
summary: One of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 7:7).

name: Jerimoth
summary: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Jerimoth
summary: 1 Chr. 27:19, ruler of Naphtali.

name: Jerimoth
summary: One of David’s sons (2 Chr. 11:18).

name: Jerimoth
summary: A Levite, one of the overseers of the temple offerings (2 Chr. 31:13) in the reign of Hezekiah.

name: Jeroham
summary: 1 Chr. 9:8; a Benjamite.

name: Jeroham
summary: 1 Chr. 12:7; a Benjamite.

name: Jeroham
summary: The father of Azareel, the “captain” of the tribe of Dan (1 Chr. 27:22).

name: Jeroham
summary: 2 Chr. 23:1; one whose son assisted in placing Joash on the throne.

name: Jerubbesheth
summary: Contender with the shame; i.e., idol, a surname also of Gideon (2 Sam. 11:21).

name: Jesaiah
summary: One of the three sons of Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

name: Jeshaiah
summary: Son of Athaliah (Ezra 8:7).

name: Jeshebeab
summary: Seat of his father, the head of the fourteenth division of priests (1 Chr. 24:13).

name: Jesher
summary: Uprightness, the first of the three sons of Caleb by Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

name: Jeshua
summary: A Levite appointed by Hezekiah to distribute offerings in the priestly cities (2 Chr. 31:15).

name: Jeshua
summary: A Levite (Ezra 8:33).

name: Jeshua
summary: Son of Kadmiel (Neh. 12:24).

name: Jesus
summary: A Jewish Christian surnamed Justus (Col. 4:11). Je’sus, the proper, as Christ is the official, name of our Lord. To distinguish him from others so called, he is spoken of as “Jesus of Nazareth” (John 18:7), and “Jesus the son of Joseph” (John 6:42). This is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua, which was originally Hoshea (Num. 13:8, 16), but changed by Moses into Jehoshua (Num. 13:16; 1 Chr. 7:27), or Joshua. After the Exile it assumed the form Jeshua, whence the Greek form Jesus. It was given to our Lord to denote the object of his mission, to save (Matt. 1:21). The life of Jesus on earth may be divided into two great periods, (1) that of his private life, till he was about thirty…

name: Jether
summary: The oldest of Gideon’s seventy sons (Judg. 8:20).

name: Jether
summary: 1 Chr. 2:32; one of Judah’s posterity.

name: Jeuel
summary: Snatched away by God, a descendant of Zerah (1 Chr. 9:6).

name: Jeush
summary: A son of Bilhan, grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10).

name: Jeush
summary: One of the three sons of Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:19).

name: Jeziel
summary: Assembled by God, a son of Azmaveth. He was one of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Joah
summary: One of the sons of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), a Korhite porter.

name: Joah
summary: Son of Joahaz, and “recorder” (q.v.) or keeper of the state archives under King Josiah (2 Chr. 34:8).

name: Joahaz
summary: (2 Chr. 34:8), a contracted form of Jehoahaz (q.v.).

name: Joanna
summary: The grandson of Zerubbabel, in the lineage of Christ (Luke 3:27); the same as Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:19).

name: Joash
summary: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Joash
summary: One who had charge of the royal stores of oil under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:28).

name: Jobab
summary: A Canaanitish king (Josh. 11:1) who joined the confederacy against Joshua.

name: Joel
summary: One of David’s famous warriors (1 Chr. 11:38).

name: Joelah
summary: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:7).

name: Joezer
summary: Jehovah is his help, one of the Korhites who became part of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 12:6).

name: Johanan
summary: The oldest of King Josiah’s sons (1 Chr. 3:15).

name: Johanan
summary: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in the desert of Judah (1 Chr. 12:12).

name: John (Relative of the High Priest)
summary: One who, with Annas and Caiaphas, sat in judgment on the apostles Peter and John (Acts 4:6). He was of the kindred of the high priest; otherwise unknown.

name: Joiarib
summary: Ezra 8:16, a “man of understanding” whom Ezra sent to “bring ministers for the house of God.”

name: Joiarib
summary: Neh. 11:5; a descendant of Judah.

name: Jokim
summary: Whom Jehovah has set up, one of the descendants of Shelah (1 Chr. 4:22).

name: Jonathan
summary: A Levite descended from Gershom (Judg. 18:30). His history is recorded in 17:7-13 and 18:30. The Rabbins changed this name into Manasseh “to screen the memory of the great lawgiver from the stain of having so unworthy an apostate among his near descendants.” He became priest of the idol image at Dan, and this office continued in his family till the Captivity.

name: Josabad
summary: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

name: Joseph (son of Judah)
summary: The son of Judah, and father of Semei (Luke 3:26). Other two of the same name in the ancestry of Christ are also mentioned (3:24, 30).

name: Jubal
summary: Jubilee, music, Lamech’s second son by Adah, of the line of Cain. He was the inventor of “the harp” (Heb. kinnor, properly “lyre”) and “the organ” (Heb. ‘ugab, properly “mouth-organ” or Pan’s pipe), Gen. 4:21.

name: Juda
summary: The father of Simeon in Christ’s maternal ancestry (Luke 3:30).

name: Judas (Jew of Damascus)
summary: A Jew of Damascus (Acts 9:11), to whose house Ananias was sent. The street called “Straight” in which it was situated is identified with the modern “street of bazaars,” where is still pointed out the so-called “house of Judas.”

name: Julia
summary: A Christian woman at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutations (Rom. 16:15), supposed to be the wife of Philologus.

name: Junia
summary: (Rom. 16:7), a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sends salutations along with Andronicus.

name: Justus
summary: A Jewish proselyte at Corinth, in whose house, next door to the synagogue, Paul held meetings and preached after he left the synagogue (Acts 18:7).

name: Kemuel
summary: The third son of Nahor (Gen. 22:21).

name: Kemuel
summary: Son of Shiphtan, appointed on behalf of the tribe of Ephraim to partition the land of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

name: Kemuel
summary: A Levite (1 Chr. 27:17).

name: Kenaz
summary: Caleb’s grandson (1 Chr. 4:15).

name: Keren-happuch
summary: Horn of the face-paint = cosmetic-box, the name of Job’s third daughter (Job. 42:14), born after prosperity had returned to him.

name: Kish
summary: A Levite in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Kish
summary: The great-grandfather of Mordecai (Esther 2:5).

name: Kore
summary: A Levitical porter at the east gate of the temple (2 Chr. 31:14).

name: Lapidoth
summary: Torches. Deborah is called “the wife of Lapidoth” (Judg. 4:4). Some have rendered the expression “a woman of a fiery spirit,” under the supposition that Lapidoth is not a proper name, a woman of a torch-like spirit.

name: Leummim
summary: Peoples; nations, the last mentioned of the three sons of Dedan, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:3).

name: Levi
summary: Luke 3:24.

name: Levi
summary: The father of Matthat, and son of Simeon, of the ancestors of Christ (Luke 3:29).

name: Lo-ammi
summary: Not my people, a symbolical name given by God’s command to Hosea’s second son in token of Jehovah’s rejection of his people (Hos. 1:9, 10), his treatment of them as a foreign people. This Hebrew word is rendered by “not my people” in ver. 10; 2:23.

name: Lois
summary: The maternal grandmother of Timothy. She is commended by Paul for her faith (2 Tim. 1:5).

name: Lucifer
summary: Brilliant star, a title given to the king of Babylon (Isa. 14:12) to denote his glory.

name: Lysanias
summary: Tetrarch of Abilene (Luke 3:1), on the eastern slope of Anti-Lebanon, near the city of Damascus.

name: Maachah
summary: The father of Hanan, who was one of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 11:43).

name: Maaseiah
summary: One of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in restoring king Jehoash to the throne (2 Chr. 23:1).

name: Maaseiah
summary: One who was sent by king Josiah to repair the temple (2 Chr. 34:8). He was governor (Heb. sar, rendered elsewhere in the Authorized Version “prince,” “chief captain,” chief ruler”) of Jerusalem.

name: Maath
summary: Small, a person named in our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:26).

name: Maaziah
summary: The head of the twenty-fourth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:18) in David’s reign.

name: Mahalaleel
summary: Neh. 11:4, a descendant of Perez.

name: Mahalath
summary: The daughter of Jerimoth, who was one of David’s sons. She was one of Rehoboam’s wives (2 Chr. 11:18).

name: Mahath
summary: Another Kohathite Levite, of the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Mahol
summary: Dance, the father of four sons (1 Kings 4:31) who were inferior in wisdom only to Solomon.

name: Malachi
summary: Messenger or angel, the last of the minor prophets, and the writer of the last book of the Old Testament canon (Mal. 4:4, 5, 6). Nothing is known of him beyond what is contained in his book of prophecies. Some have supposed that the name is simply a title descriptive of his character as a messenger of Jehovah, and not a proper name. There is reason, however, to conclude that Malachi was the ordinary name of the prophet. He was contemporary with Nehemiah (comp. Mal. 2:8 with Neh. 13:15; Mal. 2:10-16 with Neh. 13:23). No allusion is made to him by Ezra, and he does not mention the restoration of the temple, and hence it is inferred that he prophesied after Haggai and Zechariah, and when the…

name: Malchiah
summary: A priest who stood by Ezra when he “read in the book of the law of God” (Neh. 8:4).

name: Malchijah
summary: The head of the fifth division of the priests in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:9).

name: Malchijah
summary: One of the priests appointed as musicians to celebrate the completion of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

name: Malchus
summary: Reigning, the personal servant or slave of the high priest Caiaphas. He is mentioned only by John. Peter cut off his right ear in the garden of Gethsemane (John 18:10). But our Lord cured it with a touch (Matt. 26:51; Mark 14:47; Luke 22:51). This was the last miracle of bodily cure wrought by our Lord. It is not mentioned by John.

name: Malluch
summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:44).

name: Malluch
summary: Ezra 10:29.

name: Malluch
summary: Ezra 10:32

name: Manaen
summary: Consoler, a Christian teacher at Antioch. Nothing else is known of him beyond what is stated in Acts 13:1, where he is spoken of as having been brought up with (Gr. syntrophos; rendered in R.V. “foster brother” of) Herod, i.e., Herod Antipas, the tetrach, who, with his brother Archelaus, was educated at Rome.

name: Mary (Mother of John Mark)
summary: Mary the mother of John Mark was one of the earliest of our Lord’s disciples. She was the sister of Barnabas (Col. 4:10), and joined with him in disposing of their land and giving the proceeds of the sale into the treasury of the Church (Acts 4:37; 12:12). Her house in Jerusalem was the common meeting-place for the disciples there.

name: Mary (of Rome)
summary: A Christian at Rome who treated Paul with special kindness (Rom. 16:6).

name: Mattan
summary: The father of Shephatiah (Jer. 38:1).

name: Mattaniah
summary: A Levite who assisted in purifying the temple at the reformation under Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

name: Mattathias
summary: The son of Amos, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:25).

name: Mattathias
summary: The son of Semei, in the same genealogy (Luke 3:26).

name: Matthan
summary: The son of Eleazar, and father of Jacob, who was the father of Joseph, the husband of the Virgin Mary (Matt. 1:15).

name: Matthat
summary: The son of Levi, and father of Heli (Luke 3:24).

name: Matthat
summary: Son of another Levi (Luke 3:29).

name: Mattithiah
summary: The eldest son of Shallum, of the family of Korah (1 Chr. 9:31).

name: Mattithiah
summary: One who stood by Ezra while reading the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Mehetabeel
summary: Whose benefactor is God, the father of Delaiah, and grandfather of Shemaiah, who joined Sanballat against Nehemiah (Neh. 6:10).

name: Mehujael
summary: Smitten by God, the son of Irad, and father of Methusael (Gen. 4:18).

name: Mehuman
summary: Faithful, one of the eunchs whom Ahasuerus (Xerxes) commanded to bring in Vashti (Esther 1:10).

name: Melchi
summary: Luke 3:24.

name: Melchi
summary: The son of Addi, and father of Neri (Luke 3:28).

name: Melea
summary: Fulness, the son of Menan and father of Eliakim, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

name: Mephibosheth
summary: The name of Saul’s son by the concubine Rizpah (q.v.), the daughter of Aiah. He and his brother Armoni were with five others “hanged on a hill before the Lord” by the Gibeonites, and their bodies exposed in the sun for five months (2 Sam. 21:8-10).

name: Meraiah
summary: Resistance, a chief priest, a contemporary of the high priest Joiakim (Neh. 12:12).

name: Merodach-baladan
summary: Merodach has given a son, (Isa. 39:1), “the hereditary chief of the Chaldeans, a small tribe at that time settled in the marshes at the mouth of the Euphrates, but in consequence of his conquest of Babylon afterwards, they became the dominant caste in Babylonia itself.” One bearing this name sent ambassadors to Hezekiah (B.C. 721). He is also called Berodach-baladan (2 Kings 20:12; 2 Chr. 20:31).

name: Mesha
summary: Heb. id, a king of Moab, the son of Chemosh-Gad, a man of great wealth in flocks and herds (2 Kings 3:4). After the death of Ahab at Ramoth-Gilead, Mesha shook off the yoke of Israel; but on the ascension of Jehoram to the throne of Israel, that king sought the help of Jehoshaphat in an attempt to reduce the Moabites again to their former condition. The united armies of the two kings came unexpectedly on the army of the Moabites, and gained over them an easy victory. The whole land was devastated by the conquering armies, and Mesha sought refuge in his last stronghold, Kir-harasheth (q.v.). Reduced to despair, he ascended the wall of the city, and there, in the sight of the allied armies,…

name: Mesha
summary: Heb. meysh’a, “deliverance,” the eldest son of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:42), and brother of Jerahmeel.

name: Meshillemoth
summary: The father of Berechiah (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Meshullam
summary: Grandfather of Shaphan, “the scribe,” in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:3).

name: Meshullam
summary: One of the chief Gadites in Bashan in the time of Jotham (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Meshullam
summary: One of the principal Israelites who supported Ezra when expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:4).

name: Meshullam
summary: A chief priest (Neh. 12:16).

name: Meshullemeth
summary: Friend, the wife of Manasseh, and the mother of Amon (2 Kings 21:19), Kings of Judah.

name: Methusael
summary: Champion of El; man of God, a descendant of Cain (Gen. 4:18), so called, perhaps, to denote that even among the descendants of Cain God had not left himself without a witness.

name: Mibhar
summary: Choice, a Hagarene, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:38); called also Bani the Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

name: Mibsam
summary: A son of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:25).

name: Micah
summary: A descendant of Joel the Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:5).

name: Michael
summary: The father of Sethur, the spy selected to represent Asher (Num. 13:13).

name: Michael
summary: A chief Gadite in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Michael
summary: A Gershonite Levite (1 Chr. 6:40).

name: Michael
summary: 1 Chr. 7:3, a chief of the tribe of Issachar.

name: Michael
summary: 1 Chr. 8:16, a Benjamite.

name: Michael
summary: A Manassite, “a captain of thousands” who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Michael
summary: The father of Omri (1 Chr. 27:18).

name: Michael
summary: One of the sons of king Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 21:2, 4). He was murdered by his brother Jehoram.

name: Michaiah
summary: One of those sent out by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Michaiah
summary: A priest (Neh. 12:41).

name: Michri
summary: Prize of Jehovah, a Benjamite, the father of Uzzi (1 Chr. 9:8).

name: Mikloth
summary: An officer under Dodai, in the time of David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:4).

name: Milalai
summary: Eloquent, a Levitical musician (Neh. 12:36) who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.

name: Miriam
summary: 1 Chr. 4:17, one of the descendants of Judah.

name: Misham
summary: Their cleansing or their beholding, a Benjamite, one of the sons of Elpaal (1 Chr. 8:12).

name: Mishmannah
summary: Fatness, one of the Gadite heroes who gathered to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:10).

name: Mithredath
summary: The “treasurer” of King Cyrus (Ezra 1:8).

name: Mnason
summary: Reminding, or remembrancer, a Christian of Jerusalem with whom Paul lodged (Acts 21:16). He was apparently a native of Cyprus, like Barnabas (11:19, 20), and was well known to the Christians of Caesarea (4:36). He was an “old disciple” (R.V., “early disciple”), i.e., he had become a Christian in the beginning of the formation of the Church in Jerusalem.

name: Moza
summary: One of the sons of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:46).

name: Naam
summary: Pleasantness, one of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

name: Naamah (line of Cain)
summary: The daughter of Lamech and Zillah (Gen. 4: 22).

name: Naarai
summary: Youthful, a military chief in David’s army (1 Chr. 11:37), called also Paarai (2 Sam. 23:35).

name: Nahash
summary: The father of Amasa, who was commander-in-chief of Abasolom’s army (2 Sam. 17:25). Jesse’s wife had apparently been first married to this man, to whom she bore Abigail and Zeruiah, who were thus David’s sisters, but only on the mother’s side (1 Chr. 2:16).

name: Nahath
summary: A Levite, one of the overseers of the sacred offerings of the temple (2 Chr. 31:13).

name: Nahbi
summary: Hidden, one of the twelve spies sent out to explore the land of Canaan (Num. 13:14).

name: Narcissus
summary: Daffodil, a Roman whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:11). He is supposed to have been the private secretary of the emperor Claudius. This is, however, quite uncertain.

name: Nathan
summary: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14). He was charged with the education of Solomon (12:25), at whose inauguration to the throne he took a prominent part (1 Kings 1:8, 10, 11, 22-45). His two sons, Zabad (1 Chr. 2:36) and Azariah (1 Kings 4:5) occupied places of honour at the king’s court. He last appears in assisting David in reorganizing the public worship (2 Chr. 29:25). He seems to have written a life of David, and also a life of Solomon (1 Chr. 29:29; 2 Chr.…

name: Nathan
summary: Ezra 8:16.

name: Nebushasban
summary: Adorer of Nebo, or Nebo saves me, the “Rabsaris,” or chief chamberlain, of the court of Babylon. He was one of those whom the king sent to release Jeremiah from prison in Jerusalem (Jer. 39:13).

name: Nedabiah
summary: Moved of Jehovah, one of the sons of Jeconiah (1 Chr. 3:18).

name: Nehushta
summary: Copper, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem, and the wife of Jehoiakin (2 Kings 24:8), king of Judah.

name: Nemuel
summary: A Reubenite, a son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram (Num. 26:9).

name: Nethaneel
summary: One of David’s brothers (1 Chr. 2:14).

name: Nethaneel
summary: A priest who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Nethaneel
summary: A temple porter, of the family of the Korhites (1 Chr. 26:4).

name: Nethaneel
summary: One of the “princes” appointed by Jehoshaphat to teach the law through the cities of Judah (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Nethaneel
summary: A chief Levite in the time of Josiah (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Nethaneel
summary: Ezra 10:22.

name: Nethaneel
summary: A priest’s son who bore a trumpet at the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:36).

name: Nethaniah
summary: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Nicanor
summary: Conqueror, one of the seven deacons appointed in the apostolic Church (Acts 6:1-6). Nothing further is known of him.

name: Nicolas
summary: The victory of the people, a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven deacons (Acts 6:5).

name: Noadiah
summary: A Levite who returned from Babylon (Ezra 8:33).

name: Noadiah
summary: A false prophetess who assisted Tobiah and Sanballat against the Jews (Neh. 6:14). Being bribed by them, she tried to stir up discontent among the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and so to embarrass Nehemiah in his great work of rebuilding the ruined walls of the city.

name: Obadiah
summary: A chief of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:3).

name: Obadiah
summary: A Gadite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:9).

name: Obadiah
summary: A prince of Zebulun in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:19).

name: Obadiah
summary: One of the princes sent by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Obadiah
summary: A Levite who superintended the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

name: Obadiah
summary: One who accompanied Ezra on the return from Babylon (Ezra 8:9).

name: Obil
summary: A keeper of camels, an Ishmaelite who was “over the camels” in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:30).

name: Oded
summary: A prophet in the time of Ahaz and Pekah (2 Chr. 28:9-15).

name: Ohel
summary: A house; tent, the fourth son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Olympas
summary: A Roman Christian whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:15).

name: Ophrah
summary: A fawn. 1 Chr. 4:14.

name: Oren
summary: Ash or pine, the son of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25).

name: Othni
summary: A lion of Jehovah, a son of Shemaiah, and one of the temple porters in the time of David (1 Chr. 26:7). He was a “mighty man of valour.”

name: Ozem
summary: One of David’s brothers; the sixth son of Jesse (1 Chr. 2:15).

name: Ozem
summary: A son of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25).

name: Paarai
summary: Opening of the Lord, “the Arbite,” one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:35); called also Naarai, 1 Chr. 11:37.

name: Palti
summary: Deliverance from the Lord, one of the spies representing the tribe of Benjamin (Num. 13:9).

name: Paltiel
summary: Deliverance of God, the prince of Issachar who assisted “to divide the land by inheritance” (Num. 34:26).

name: Parmashta
summary: Strong-fisted, a son of Haman, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:9).

name: Parmenas
summary: Constant, one of the seven “deacons” (Acts 6:5).

name: Parshandatha
summary: An interpreter of the law, the eldest of Haman’s sons, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:7).

name: Paruah
summary: Flourishing, the father of Jehoshaphat, appointed to provide monthly supplies for Solomon from the tribe of Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

name: Pasach
summary: Clearing, one of the sons of Japhlet, of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:33).

name: Patrobas
summary: A Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

name: Pedahel
summary: Redeemed of God, the son of Ammihud, a prince of Naphtali (Num. 34:28).

name: Pedaiah
summary: The father of Zebudah, who was the wife of Josiah and mother of king Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

name: Pedaiah
summary: . The father of Joel, ruler of the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chr. 27:20).

name: Pelaiah
summary: One of David’s posterity (1 Chr. 3:24).

name: Pelatiah
summary: A son of Hananiah and grandson of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:21).

name: Pelet
summary: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:47).

name: Pelet
summary: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Peleth
summary: A Reubenite whose son was one of the conspirators against Moses and Aaron (Num. 16:1).

name: Peleth
summary: One of the sons of Jonathan (1 Chr. 2:33).

name: Persis
summary: A female Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:12). She is spoken of as “beloved,” and as having “laboured much in the Lord.”

name: Pethahiah
summary: The chief of one of the priestly courses (the nineteenth) in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:16).

name: Pethahiah
summary: A Levite (Ezra 10:23).

name: Pethahiah
summary: A descendant of Judah who had some office at the court of Persia (Neh. 11:24).

name: Pethuel
summary: Vision of God, the father of Joel the prophet (Joel 1:1).

name: Peulthai
summary: Wages of the Lord, one of the sons of Obed-edom, a Levite porter (1 Chr. 26:5).

name: Phanuel
summary: Face of God, father of the prophetess Anna (q.v.), Luke 2:36.

name: Pharaoh
summary: The Pharaoh of 1 Chr. 4:18.

name: Phebe
summary: A “deaconess of the church at Cenchrea,” the port of Corinth. She was probably the bearer of Paul’s epistle to the Romans. Paul commended her to the Christians at Rome; “for she hath been,” says he, “a succourer of many, and of myself also” (Rom. 16:1, 2).

name: Philemon
summary: An inhabitant of Colosse, and apparently a person of some note among the citizens (Col. 4:9; Philemon 1:2). He was brought to a knowledge of the gospel through the instrumentality of Paul (19), and held a prominent place in the Christian community for his piety and beneficence (4-7). He is called in the epistle a “fellow-labourer,” and therefore probably held some office in the church at Colosse; at all events, the title denotes that he took part in the work of spreading a knowledge of the gospel.

name: Philetus
summary: Amiable, with Hymenaeus, at Ephesus, said that the “resurrection was past already” (2 Tim. 2:17, 18). This was a Gnostic heresy held by the Nicolaitanes.

name: Phlegon
summary: Burning, a Roman Christian to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

name: Phygellus
summary: Fugitive, a Christian of Asia, who “turned away” from Paul during his second imprisonment at Rome (2 Tim. 1:15). Nothing more is known of him.

name: Puah
summary: One of the two midwives who feared God, and refused to kill the Hebrew male children at their birth (Ex. 1:15-21).

name: Puah
summary: A descendant of Issachar (Judg. 10:1).

name: Pudens
summary: Bashful, a Christian at Rome, who sent his greetings to Timothy (2 Tim. 4:21).

name: Quartus
summary: Fourth, a Corinthian Christian who sent by Paul his salutations to friends at Rome (Rom. 16:23).

name: Rabsaris
summary: Chief of the Heads, one of the three officers whom Sennacherib sent from Lachish with a threatening message to Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17; Jer. 39:3, 13).

name: Rachab
summary: '=Rahab, a name found in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:5).

name: Raham
summary: Merciful, one of the descendants of Caleb, the son of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:44).

name: Ram
summary: A person mentioned in Job 32:2 as founder of a clan to which Elihu belonged. The same as Aram of Gen. 22:21.

name: Raphu
summary: Healed, a Benjamite, whose son Palti was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:9).

name: Regem-melech
summary: Friend of the king, one of the two messengers sent by the exiled Jews to Jerusalem in the time of Darius (Zech. 7:2) to make inquiries at the temple.

name: Rehum
summary: A Levite (Neh. 3:17).

name: Rei
summary: Friendly, one who maintained true allegiance to king David (1 Kings 1:8) when Adonijah rebelled.

name: Rephael
summary: Healed of God, one of Shemaiah’s sons. He and his brethren, on account of their “strength for service,” formed one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:7, 8).

name: Rezon
summary: Prince, son of Eliadah. Abandoning the service of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah, on the occasion of his being defeated by David, he became the “captain over a band” of marauders, and took Damascus, and became king of Syria (1 Kings 11:23-25; 2 Sam. 8:3-8). For centuries after this the Syrians were the foes of Israel. He “became an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon.”

name: Rhesa
summary: Affection, son of Zorobabel, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:27).

name: Rhoda
summary: A rose, the damsel in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark. She came to hearken when Peter knocked at the door of the gate (Acts 12:12-15).

name: Sacar
summary: A son of Obed-edom the Gittite, and a temple porter (1 Chr. 26:4).

name: Sadoc
summary: Just, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:14).

name: Salathiel
summary: Whom I asked of God, the son of Jeconiah (Matt. 1:12; 1 Chr. 3:17); also called the son of Neri (Luke 3:27). The probable explanation of the apparent discrepancy is that he was the son of Neri, the descendant of Nathan, and thus heir to the throne of David on the death of Jeconiah (comp. Jer. 22:30).

name: Sallai
summary: A Benjamite (Neh. 11:8).

name: Samgar-nebo
summary: Be gracious, O Nebo! or a cup-bearer of Nebo, probably the title of Nergal-sharezer, one of the princes of Babylon (Jer. 39:3).

name: Sapphira
summary: Beautiful, the wife of Ananias (q.v.). She was a partner in his guilt and also in his punishment (Acts 5:1-11).

name: Sceva
summary: An implement, a Jew, chief of the priests at Ephesus (Acts 19:13-16); i.e., the head of one of the twenty-four courses of the house of Levi. He had seven sons, who “took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus,” in imitation of Paul. They tried their method of exorcism on a fierce demoniac, and failed. His answer to them was to this effect (19:15): “The Jesus whom you invoke is One whose authority I acknowledge; and the Paul whom you name I recognize to be a servant or messenger of God; but what sort of men are ye who have been empowered to act as you do by neither?” (Lindsay on the Acts of the Apostles.)

name: Secundus
summary: Second, a Christian of Thessalonica who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4).

name: Segub
summary: The youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite. His death is recorded in 1 Kings 16:34 (comp. Josh. 6:26).

name: Semei
summary: Mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:26).

name: Seorim
summary: Barley, the chief of the forth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:8).

name: Seraiah
summary: The grandfather of Jehu (1 Chr. 4:35).

name: Sergius Paulus
summary: A “prudent man” (R.V., “man of understanding”), the deputy (R.V., “proconsul”) of Cyprus (Acts 13:6-13). He became a convert to Christianity under Paul, who visited this island on his first mission to the heathen. A remarkable memorial of this proconsul was recently (1887) discovered at Rome. On a boundary stone of Claudius his name is found, among others, as having been appointed (A.D. 47) one of the curators of the banks and the channel of the river Tiber. After serving his three years as proconsul at Cyprus, he returned to Rome, where he held the office referred to. As he is not saluted in Paul’s letter to the Romans, he probably died before it was written.

name: Sethur
summary: Hidden, one of the spies sent to search the Promised Land. He was of the tribe of Asher (Num. 13:13).

name: Shaashgaz
summary: Servant of the beautiful, a chief eunuch in the second house of the harem of king Ahasuerus (Esther 2:14).

name: Shallum
summary: A descendant of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:25).

name: Shallum
summary: An Ephraimite chief (2 Chr. 28:12).

name: Shallum
summary: The uncle of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer. 32:7).

name: Shamir
summary: One of the sons of Michah (1 Chr. 24:24).

name: Shammah
summary: One of David’s three mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11, 12).

name: Shammua
summary: One of the spies sent out by Moses to search the land (Num. 13:4). He represented the tribe of Reuben.

name: Shaphat
summary: One of the spies. He represented the tribe of Simeon (Num. 13:5).

name: Shaphat
summary: One of David’s chief herdsmen (1 Chr. 27:29).

name: Shebaniah
summary: A Levite appointed to blow the trumpet before the ark of God (1 Chr. 15:24).

name: Shebaniah
summary: A priest (Neh. 10:12).

name: Shecaniah
summary: A priest to whom the tenth lot came forth when David divided the priests (1 Chr. 24:11).

name: Shecaniah
summary: One of the priests who were set “to give to their brethren by courses” of the daily portion (2 Chr. 31:15). Shechani’ah, id.

name: Shechaniah
summary: Ezra 8:5.

name: Shechaniah
summary: The father-in-law of Tobiah (Neh. 6:18).

name: Shelemiah
summary: Ezra 10:39.

name: Shelemiah
summary: The father of Hananiah (Neh. 3:30).

name: Shelemiah
summary: Father of a captain of the ward (Jer. 37:13).

name: Shema
summary: A Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:8).

name: Shema
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:13).

name: Shema
summary: One who stood by Ezra when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Shemaah
summary: Rumour, a Benjamite whose sons “came to David to Ziklag” (1 Chr. 12:3).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A Levite (1 Chr. 24:6).

name: Shemaiah
summary: One of the Levites whom Jehoshaphat appointed to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A Levite (2 Chr. 29:14).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A Levite appointed to “distribute the oblations of the Lord” (2 Chr. 31:15).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A Levite (2 Chr. 35:9).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A false prophet who hindered the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Neh. 6:10).

name: Shemaiah
summary: A priest (Neh. 12:42).

name: Shemaiah
summary: The father of Urijah the prophet (Jer. 26:20).

name: Shemaiah
summary: The father of a prince in the reign of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

name: Shemariah
summary: One who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Shemeber
summary: Soaring on high, the king of Zeboiim, who joined with the other kings in casting off the yoke of Chedorlaomer. After having been reconquered by him, he was rescued by Abraham (Gen. 14:2).

name: Shemiramoth
summary: A Levite in the reign of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Shemuel
summary: The son of Ammihud. He represented Simeon in the division of the land (Num. 34:20).

name: Shemuel
summary: A prince of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:2).

name: Shephatiah
summary: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Shephatiah
summary: A Simeonite prince in David’s time (1 Chr. 27:16).

name: Shephatiah
summary: One of Jehoshaphat’s sons (2 Chr. 21:2).

name: Shephatiah
summary: One of the princes who urged the putting of Jeremiah to death (Jer. 38:1-4).

name: Sheresh
summary: Root, a descendant of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:16).

name: Sherezer
summary: One of the messengers whom the children of the Captivity sent to Jerusalem “to pray for them before the Lord” (Zech. 7:2).

name: Shethar
summary: A star, a prince at the court of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:14).

name: Sheva
summary: The son of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:49).

name: Shimea
summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:30).

name: Shimea
summary: Another Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:39).

name: Shimeah
summary: A Benjamite, a descendant of Gibeon (1 Chr. 8:32); called also Shimeam (9:38).

name: Shimei
summary: A Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:42).

name: Shimei
summary: A son of Pedaiah, the brother of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19).

name: Shimei
summary: A Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:4).

name: Shimei
summary: A Ramathite who was “over the vineyards” of David (1 Chr. 27:27).

name: Shimei
summary: One of the sons of Heman, who assisted in the purification of the temple (2 Chr. 29:14).

name: Shimeon
summary: Hearkening. Ezra 10:31.

name: Shimhi
summary: Famous, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:21).

name: Shimri
summary: A Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Shimri
summary: The father of one of the “valiant men” of David’s armies (1 Chr. 11:45).

name: Shimri
summary: Assisted at the purification of the temple in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

name: Shinab
summary: Cooling, the king of Adamah, in the valley of Siddim, who with his confederates was conquered by Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

name: Shiphrah
summary: Beauty, one of the Egyptian midwives (Ex. 1:15).

name: Shiphtan
summary: Judicial, an Ephraimite prince at the time of the division of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

name: Shobab
summary: One of the sons of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:18), the son of Hezron.

name: Shobi
summary: Captor, son of Nahash of Rabbah, the Ammonite. He showed kindness to David when he fled from Jerusalem to Mahanaim (2 Sam. 17:27).

name: Shua
summary: A daughter of Heber the Asherite (1 Chr. 7:32).

name: Simeon
summary: One of the ancestors of Joseph (Luke 3:30).

name: Simeon
summary: Surnamed Niger, i.e., “black,” perhaps from his dark complexion, a teacher of some distinction in the church of Antioch (Acts 13:1-3). It has been supposed that this was the Simon of Cyrene who bore Christ’s cross. Note the number of nationalities represented in the church at Antioch.

name: Simri
summary: Watchman, a Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 26:10).

name: So
summary: (Nubian, Sabako), an Ethiopian king who brought Egypt under his sway. He was bribed by Hoshea to help him against the Assyrian monarch Shalmaneser (2 Kings 17:4). This was a return to the policy that had been successful in the reign of Jeroboam I.

name: Stachys
summary: Spike; an ear of corn, a convert at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:9).

name: Susanna
summary: Lily, with other pious women, ministered to Jesus (Luke 8:3).

name: Susi
summary: The father of Gaddi, who was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:11).

name: Syntyche
summary: Fortunate; affable, a female member of the church at Philippi, whom Paul beseeches to be of one mind with Euodias (Phil. 4:2, 3).

name: Tabeal
summary: Goodness of God, the father of one whom the kings of Syria and Samaria in vain attempted to place on the throne of Ahaz (Isa. 7:6).

name: Tabeel
summary: A Persian governor of Samaria, who joined others in the attempt to prevent the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Ezra 4:7).

name: Tabrimon
summary: Good is Rimmon, the father of Benhadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

name: Tamar
summary: A daughter of Absalom (2 Sam. 14:27).

name: Temeni
summary: One of the sons of Ashur, the father of Tekoa (1 Chr. 4:6).

name: Thahash
summary: A badger, a son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother (Gen. 22:24).

name: Theudas
summary: Thanksgiving, referred to by Gamaliel in his speech before the council at Jerusalem (Acts 5:36). He headed an insurrection against the Roman authority. Beyond this nothing is known of him.

name: Tiberius
summary: I.e., as known in Roman history, Tiberius Claudius Nero, only mentioned in Luke 3:1. He was the stepson of Augustus, whom he succeeded on the throne, A.D. 14. He was noted for his vicious and infamous life. In the fifteenth year of his reign John the Baptist entered on his public ministry, and under him also our Lord taught and suffered. He died A.D. 37. He is frequently referred to simply as “Caesar” (Matt. 22:17, 21; Mark 12:14, 16, 17; Luke 20:22, 24, 25; 23:2; John 19:12, 15).

name: Timaeus
summary: Defiled, the father of blind Bartimaeus (Mark 10:46).

name: Timon
summary: Honouring, one of the seven deacons at Jerusalem (Acts 6:5). Nothing further is known of him.

name: Tobadonijah
summary: Good is Jehovah, my Lord, a Levite sent out by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people of Judah in the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Tobijah
summary: Id., a Levite sent out through Judah by Jehoshaphat to teach the people (2 Chr. 17:8).

name: Tola
summary: A judge of the tribe of Issachar who “judged” Israel twenty-three years (Judg. 10:1, 2), when he died, and was buried in Shamir. He was succeeded by Jair.

name: Tubal-cain
summary: The son of Lamech and Zillah, “an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron” (Gen. 4:22; R.V., “the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron”).

name: Tyrannus
summary: Prince, a Greek rhetorician, in whose “school” at Ephesus Paul disputed daily for the space of two years with those who came to him (Acts 19:9). Some have supposed that he was a Jew, and that his “school” was a private synagogue.

name: Ucal
summary: The name of a person to whom Agur’s words are addressed (Prov. 30:1).

name: Unni
summary: A Levite who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 12:9).

name: Uriel
summary: The father of Michaiah, one of Rehoboam’s wives, and mother of Abijah (2 Chr. 13:2).

name: Urijah
summary: One of the priests who stood at the right hand of Ezra’s pulpit when he read and expounded the law (Neh. 8:4).

name: Uzzi
summary: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

name: Uzzi
summary: A Benjamite, a chief in the tribe (1 Chr. 9:8).

name: Uzzi
summary: A son of Bani. He had the oversight of the Levites after the return from captivity (Neh. 11:22).

name: Uzzi
summary: The head of the house of Jedaiah, one of “the chief of the priests” (Neh. 12:19).

name: Uzzi
summary: A priest who assisted in the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

name: Uzziah
summary: The father of Jehonathan, one of David’s overseers (1 Chr. 27:25).

name: Uzziel
summary: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

name: Uzziel
summary: A son of Jeduthan (2 Chr. 29:14).

name: Uzziel
summary: The son of Harhaiah (Neh. 3:8).

name: Vajezatha
summary: Purity; worthy of honour, one of Haman’s sons, whom the Jews slew in the palace of Shushan (Esther 9:9).

name: Zabad
summary: One of David’s valiant men (1 Chr. 11:41), the descendant of Ahlai, of the “children of Sheshan” (2:31).

name: Zabad
summary: Ezra 10:27.

name: Zabad
summary: Ezra 10:33.

name: Zabad
summary: Ezra 10:43.

name: Zabbai
summary: Ezra 10:28.

name: Zabbai
summary: The father of Baruch, who “earnestly repaired” part of the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:20; marg., “Zaccai”).

name: Zabbud
summary: Gift, Ezra 8:14.

name: Zabdi
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:19).

name: Zabdi
summary: Called “the Shiphmite,” one of David’s officers, who had charge of his vineyards (1 Chr. 27:27).

name: Zabdiel
summary: The father of Jashobeam, who was one of David’s officers (1 Chr. 27:2).

name: Zabdiel
summary: An overseer of the priests after the Captivity (Neh. 11:14).

name: Zabud
summary: Gift, the son of Nathan, who was “king’s friend” in the court of Solomon (1 Kings 4:5).

name: Zaccur
summary: Father of Shammua, who was one of the spies sent out by Moses (Num. 13:4).

name: Zaccur
summary: A Merarite Levite (1 Chr. 24:27).

name: Zaccur
summary: Son of Imri (Neh. 3:2).

name: Zaccur
summary: A Levite (Neh. 10:12).

name: Zaccur
summary: The son of Mattaniah (Neh. 13:13).

name: Zadok
summary: The sons of Baana, one of those who assisted in rebuilding the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:4).

name: Zadok
summary: “The scribe” set over the treasuries of the temple by Nehemiah along with a priest and a Levite (Neh. 13:13).

name: Zatthu
summary: A sprout, Neh. 10:14.

name: Zaza
summary: Plenty, a descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:33).

name: Zebadiah
summary: A son of Beriah (1 Chr. 8:15).

name: Zebadiah
summary: A Korhite porter of the Lord’s house (1 Chr. 26:2). Three or four others of this name are also mentioned.

name: Zebadiah
summary: A son of Asahel, Joab’s brother (1 Chr. 27:7).

name: Zebadiah
summary: A Levite who took part as one of the teachers in the system of national education instituted by Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:7, 8).

name: Zebadiah
summary: The son of Ishmael, “the ruler of the house of Judah in all the king’s matters” (2 Chr. 19:8-11).

name: Zebudah
summary: Given, the wife of Josiah and mother of Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

name: Zechariah
summary: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:7).

name: Zechariah
summary: A Kohathite Levite (1 Chr. 24:25).

name: Zechariah
summary: A Merarite Levite (1 Chr. 27:21).

name: Zechariah
summary: One who assisted in teaching the law to the people in the time of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:7).

name: Zechariah
summary: A Levite of the sons of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14).

name: Zechariah
summary: One of Jehoshaphat’s sons (2 Chr. 21:2).

name: Zechariah
summary: A prophet, who had “understanding in the seeing of God,” in the time of Uzziah, who was much indebted to him for his wise counsel (2 Chr. 26:5). Besides these, there is a large number of persons mentioned in Scripture bearing this name of whom nothing is known.

name: Zechariah
summary: One of the “rulers of the house of God” (2 Chr. 35:8).

name: Zedekiah
summary: The son of Hananiah, a prince of Judah in the days of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

name: Zemira
summary: Vine-dresser, a Benjamite; one of the sons of Becher (1 Chr. 7:8).

name: Zenas
summary: A disciple called “the lawyer,” whom Paul wished Titus to bring with him (Titus 3:13). Nothing more is known of him.

name: Zerah
summary: An “Ethiopian,” probably Osorkon II., the successor of Shishak on the throne of Egypt. With an enormous army, the largest we read of in Scripture, he invaded the kingdom of Judah in the days of Asa (2 Chr. 14:9-15). He reached Zephathah, and there encountered the army of Asa. This is the only instance “in all the annals of Judah of a victorious encounter in the field with a first-class heathen power in full force.” The Egyptian host was utterly routed, and the Hebrews gathered “exceeding much spoil.” Three hundred years elapsed before another Egyptian army, that of Necho (B.C. 609), came up against Jerusalem.

name: Zeruah
summary: Stricken, mother of Jeroboam, the first king of the ten tribes (1 Kings 11:26).

name: Zethan
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 7:10).

name: Zia
summary: Fear, a Gadite (1 Chr. 5:13).

name: Zibia
summary: Gazelle, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:9).

name: Zichri
summary: A Benjamite chief (1 Chr. 8:19).

name: Zichri
summary: Another of the same tribe (1 Chr. 8:23).

name: Zidkijah
summary: The Lord is righteous, one who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Neh. 10:1).

name: Ziha
summary: A ruler among the Nethinim (Neh. 11:21).

name: Zilthai
summary: A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:20).

name: Zilthai
summary: One of the captains of the tribe of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

name: Zimmah
summary: The father of Joah (2 Chr. 29:12).

name: Ziphah
summary: A descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 4:16).

name: Zithri
summary: The Lord protects, a Levite, son of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

name: Ziza
summary: A Simeonite prince (1 Chr. 4:37-43).

name: Ziza
summary: A son of Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:20).

name: Zoheth
summary: Snatching (?), one of the sons of Ishi (1 Chr. 4:20).

name: Zuriel
summary: Rock of God, chief of the family of the Merarites (Num. 3:35) at the time of the Exodus.

name: Zoar
summary: Small, a town on the east or south-east of the Dead Sea, to which Lot and his daughters fled from Sodom (Gen. 19:22, 23). It was originally called Bela (14:2, 8). It is referred to by the prophets Isaiah (15:5) and Jeremiah (48:34). Its ruins are still seen at the opening of the ravine of Kerak, the Kir-Moab referred to in 2 Kings 3, the modern Tell esh-Shaghur.
